Revises numerous municipal-election procedures and exempts municipal elections from specified voter-identification provisions. The access effect of the ID exemption is directionally permissive, while the broader package cannot be reduced from the synopsis to generic 'integrity controls.'
Amends Alabama's immigration law governing proof of legal status for government business transactions and accepts military privilege-and-identification cards. It is not an election-integrity measure.
Repeals statutory judicial-recusal provisions based on campaign-contribution thresholds, weakening a campaign-finance-related judicial conflict safeguard.

Requires electronic monitoring for specified released inmates while also providing state photo identification upon release. It combines greater correctional surveillance with a reentry-support measure and is not election-integrity legislation.

Authorizes health-care sharing ministries outside Insurance Department regulation with mandated disclaimers, favoring voluntary private risk sharing and regulatory exemption over conventional insurance oversight.

Creates strong civil enforcement against Medicaid false claims, requires Attorney General action, and protects employees from retaliation. This is public-program integrity and whistleblower policy, not a broad public-versus-private healthcare allocation rule.
Establishes a statewide integrated healthcare system for veterans and immediate family members, expanding state-organized healthcare provision for a defined population.
Requires concussion protocols, removal from play, professional clearance, and safety training for youth sports organizations, expanding health-and-safety regulation and patient protection.
Extends or strengthens the prohibition on specified public officials becoming lobbyists for two years, restricting the government-to-lobbying revolving door.

Bars public bodies from processing payroll deductions for PAC contributions or dues to membership organizations using funds politically. The burden principally restricts public-employee unions and allied membership organizations.
Constitutionalizes right-to-work policy and creates a cause of action, strengthening limits on compulsory union membership or financial support.
Preempts local governments from setting minimum wages or employment benefits, restricting local labor standards and expanding state preemption.
Constitutionalizes right-to-work policy by barring employment requirements to join or pay dues to a union.

Requires local governing-body approval before ADEM may act on a new solid-waste facility and treats failure to approve within the statutory period as denial. This strengthens local siting control and a facility-development constraint.

Removes the requirement that an industrial development authority receive fair market value when transferring its land, expanding targeted development-subsidy flexibility while weakening a public-asset safeguard.

Creates or revises criminal protections and restitution for police, search-and-rescue, and fire-service animals. It is a narrow animal-protection offense rather than a general expansion of police authority.
Repeals an antiquated time-of-day criminal prohibition on buying or selling domestic animals or fowl, reducing a narrow commercial criminal regulation rather than restricting police power generally.

Prohibits picketing or protesting in specified circumstances and imposes criminal penalties. Without fuller text the exact scope is unclear, but its ideological content is restriction of protest activity through public-order enforcement.
Expands or revises Transportation Department contracting with private firms for construction and maintenance of roads and public improvements, favoring private delivery of public works.

Authorizes loans from Escambia County's oil-and-gas severance trust for economic development and transportation infrastructure. This redirects resource revenue toward public development financing rather than expanding extraction itself.

Revises compulsory pooling, deductions, and risk-compensation charges affecting nonconsenting owners in drilling units. It facilitates collective extraction while burdening dissenting ownership interests; precise direction depends on the amended terms.

Authorizes conversion of oil-and-gas wells to alternative-energy facilities and broadens state-land energy leasing. It expands energy-development authority across technologies and is not simply fossil expansion.
Expands absentee-ballot eligibility or procedures for qualified visually impaired voters, increasing voting access for a defined disability group.
Requires TANF applicants to seek at least three unsubsidized jobs and makes applicants ineligible under specified failures, tightening work-search conditions and access to cash assistance.
Requires Alabama to seek a federal waiver barring SNAP purchases of soda and candy and provides for implementation, increasing paternalistic conditions on food assistance.

Bars state adverse action against child-placement providers acting on religious beliefs and creates civil remedies. It protects traditionalist religious agencies while permitting service exclusion that can reduce equal access, particularly for LGBTQ applicants.

Prohibits pass-through appropriations except for valid agency-program support, authorizes line items and reporting, and imposes administrative and criminal penalties. It strengthens budget accountability while restricting an appropriations practice.
Creates reduced-speed zones near schools in unincorporated areas, requires signs, and doubles fines, expanding school-safety traffic regulation and penalties.
Increases civil penalties for malicious trade-secret theft and criminalizes intentional payment of another to misappropriate trade secrets, strengthening business intellectual-property enforcement.
Specifies physical-education program requirements for public and private schools, expanding state curricular or health-program mandates; the synopsis does not show the precise requirements.
Locally reallocates increased TVA payments-in-lieu-of-taxes to the Madison County legislative delegation office. It is geographically specific and unsuitable as a general ideological signal.
Delays new base-wage eligibility requirements for already-filed economic-development incentive applications, preserving near-term access to targeted tax subsidies under prior rules.
Constitutionally prohibits an occupational tax in Madison County. It is a clear anti-tax position but local and not automatically generalizable statewide.
Adopts a uniform interstate jurisdiction and enforcement framework for adult guardianship and protective orders. The synopsis shows legal coordination rather than a clear ideological direction.
Moves the effective date of the Limited Partnership Act to coincide with the new business-entities code, a technical timing correction.
Allows the Legislature by local law to appoint alternate election officers. This changes an administrative appointment mechanism without a clear access or partisan direction in the synopsis.

Changes commodity-promotion association audits to every two years while requiring financial statements. It is technical governance of producer-approved assessments rather than a reliable ideological signal.

Creates a separate board and revises governance of Alabama's prepaid college-tuition program. It concerns public program administration; the synopsis alone does not establish expansion or retrenchment.
Establishes an advisory task force for the prepaid college-tuition program. Creating a study body alone supplies little ideological information.
Raises truck weight allowances for vehicles using auxiliary power or idle-reduction technology, removing a regulatory disincentive to fuel-saving equipment.

Creates a permanent legislative energy committee and policy office to develop a state energy plan. It expands state planning capacity but does not select a fossil, renewable, or conservation direction.
Requires source-of-funding disclosure for electioneering communications and paid political advertising and revises political-committee contribution rules.
Makes property connected to electronic child-solicitation crimes forfeitable, expanding punitive sanctions and government forfeiture authority.
Bars sex offenders from driving passenger vehicles or school buses and from obtaining the relevant commercial endorsements, backed by penalties. It expands preventive public-order restrictions.

The enrolled text permits officials to skip counting write-ins that cannot change an office's outcome, unless a voter requests a count within two business days and pays its actual cost. This restricts routine tabulation of valid write-ins and shifts the exception's cost to the requesting voter.
Directs the Board of Adjustment to approve county claims denied by agencies unless the agency used adopted written procedures, strengthening procedural protection for local reimbursement claims.

Authorizes Madison County to regulate dangerous dogs in unincorporated areas through confinement requirements and civil penalties. It is a local safety measure without a reliable statewide ideological signal.

Removes restrictive ownership and naming requirements for architecture firms while revising professional responsibility and discipline. It is principally occupational deregulation with retained oversight.

Retroactively validates municipal annexations meeting specified conditions. Without the conditions or affected places, the synopsis supports a legal-validation disposition rather than a directional land-use judgment.

Limits public release of 911 audio while allowing court-ordered, caller, and litigation access and treating written or electronic records as public writings. It trades transparency for caller privacy with controlled exceptions.
Reconstitutes the State Health Planning board and authorizes cause-based member-removal rules. The synopsis does not show a directional change in healthcare planning policy.
Limits a jointly owned property's homestead exemption to the ownership share or benefit of the qualified owner, narrowing the exemption rather than broadly changing property-tax rates.
Allows on-premises draft or keg alcohol sales in Chambers County subject to referendum. It locally liberalizes alcohol regulation with direct voter approval.
Revises trademark registration, renewal, protected goods and services, and civil remedies, strengthening or modernizing intellectual-property protection.
Allows Mobile County to set the number and districts of commissioners and establishes initial districts. It is local governmental structure whose representational effect requires maps and context.

Allows original owners to rebuild salvage vehicles and removes Revenue Department valuation approval while retaining inspections and penalties. It modestly deregulates rebuilding subject to safety and title controls.
Authorizes a secretary and compensation for the Mobile County license commissioner. This is local office administration without general ideological content.
Expands or revises seizure procedures for vehicles and equipment connected to timber theft and unauthorized harvesting, strengthening property-crime enforcement and forfeiture authority.
Makes the Dale County commission chair a separately elected countywide office rather than a probate-judge duty, subject to referendum. It is local institutional design.
Clarifies title definitions, fees, exemptions, inspections, and lien release when a lienholder has closed. It is primarily technical vehicle-title administration.

Increases compensation for municipal and county water, sewer, and fire-protection authority boards, with a local exception. This is public-board compensation rather than a public-versus-private service choice.
Limits grandparents to one visitation petition per 24 months and similarly limits parental petitions to amend or revoke awards, constraining repeated family-court litigation for both sides.

Limits division of military retired pay in divorce to a formula based on rank and pay at the final order plus then-current cost-of-living increases, constraining later increases awarded to a former spouse.
Requires all underground-facility operators to participate in the one-call system and clarifies notification duties, strengthening coordinated excavation-safety regulation.
Requires communications-district employees handling funds to be bonded, adding a narrow public-financial safeguard.
Aligns Mobile's library-board membership with the city-council membership count. It is local board structure without clear ideological direction.
Levies a Coffee County building fee to fund municipal and volunteer fire and emergency medical services, subject to referendum. It is local public-safety finance.
Allows Blount County to provide an expense allowance when an elected official voluntarily reduces salary because of retirement-plan participation. It is local compensation administration.

Prohibits short-barreled rifles or shotguns only when their possession or transfer violates federal law, with exceptions and penalties. It aligns state criminal law to the federal regulatory floor rather than creating a broader ban.
Requires or authorizes redaction of Social Security numbers and birth dates from marriage licenses and public documents, prioritizing personal privacy over unrestricted record display.
Increases allowable bus dimensions and authorizes articulated buses on state highways, relaxing vehicle-dimension rules for transit operations.
Creates a rebuttable presumption for criminal littering and expands enforcement to county license and solid-waste officers, strengthening punitive environmental enforcement.
Adopts uniform preventive and emergency procedures for credible child-abduction risks, including international cases, expanding protective family-court intervention.
Allows chiropractic scholarship funds to support specified advanced courses at in-state colleges and universities, modestly broadening an existing education subsidy.
Creates exceptions to the requirement that foreign or alien surplus-line insurers have operated for five years in their home jurisdiction, modestly relaxing insurance-market entry rules.
Allows bicyclists to signal from the right side, a technical road-safety clarification without meaningful ideological content.

Restructures PACT governance, supplies formula-based Education Trust Fund appropriations for a limited period, and establishes dissolution terms. It uses public funds to stabilize legacy tuition obligations while planning program closure.

Creates special warrant or arrest procedures for alleged offenses by public educators and law-enforcement officers committed in line of duty. It adds procedural protection for public employees, though the synopsis does not specify its extent.
Creates or adjusts an Etowah County solicitor's fee to fund the district attorney. It is local criminal-justice finance.
Constitutionally authorizes the Legislature to set Etowah County court costs by general or local law. It is a local fiscal-enabling provision.

The text limits the 16-foot-net restriction to temporarily closed or exclusive-bait areas and increases authorized baskets from one to two on a boat, two on a truck, and four at a business. It relaxes harvest and possession restrictions for licensed bait operators.
Removes an accreditation-progress condition and adds a Montgomery County institution to the Alabama Student Grant Program, broadening public grant eligibility for students at a targeted institution.
Expands out-of-state access to the prescription-monitoring database and authorizes fees for its operation, broadening controlled-substance surveillance and data sharing.
Revises election, qualification, term, compensation, and leadership rules for Hartselle's school board subject to referendum. It is local institutional design.
Allows Mobile County officers to accept credit cards and charge a cost-covering fee. It is local payment administration.
Establishes an interagency elder-abuse prevention council with reporting duties and sunset review, expanding coordinated protective-government capacity.
Requires electronic distribution and online publication of Attorney General opinions, expanding public access while replacing paper distribution.
Charges applicants for interstate adult-offender supervision transfers and dedicates the proceeds to probation upkeep, shifting supervision costs toward affected offenders.

Extends free distinctive license tags to surviving spouses of firefighters killed in the line of duty and adjusts eligibility lists. It is a narrow commemorative benefit rather than a broad ideological policy.

Modernizes building and energy codes, requires county and municipal implementation consistent with federal law, and excludes specified farm structures. It expands energy-efficiency regulation with a rural/agricultural exemption.
Exempts one named nonprofit from state and local sales and use tax. It is a targeted tax expenditure unsuitable as a general tax-position signal.
Provides a direct appropriation to Talladega College, supporting targeted public funding for a historically Black private institution.
Provides a direct appropriation to Tuskegee University, supporting targeted public funding for a historically Black private institution.
Provides a direct appropriation to Lyman Ward Military Academy, supporting targeted public funding for a private military school.

Makes annual appropriations for public education support, maintenance, and development. Direction and generosity require comparison with the prior budget, but the measure embodies public education provision.

Shifts school-bond debt service toward the Education Trust Fund, supplements swap-related debt service, reappropriates prior agency funds, and preserves federal food-assistance funds for child care. It is a mixed fiscal package with identifiable public-education and child-care funding effects.

Transfers receipts allocated to the State Board of Education from the Children First Trust Fund into the General Fund for FY2011, weakening the child-program earmark to increase general-budget flexibility.

Extends the Employment Security Enhancement Fund assessment and provides for federally financed extended unemployment compensation, combining an employer-side funding mechanism with continued unemployment support.
Provides supplemental state appropriations to two named public schools for facility support, expanding targeted public-education spending.
Allows additional members and revises terms for county and municipal library boards, modestly expanding or restructuring public-library governance.
Enacts the ordinary annual General Fund budget. Ideological direction cannot be inferred without amounts, baselines, amendments, or agency-level changes.
Appropriates funds to the Coalition Against Domestic Violence while requiring operating plans, audits, and periodic reports, combining service support with grant accountability.
Appropriates tobacco-settlement revenue through the Children First Trust Fund for FY2011, conditions allocations on receipts, and requires audits and legislative reporting.
Allows no-contest pleas to be used for impeachment, habitual-offender sentencing, and capital-murder cases, expanding the collateral and punitive use of prior pleas.
Strengthens recycler records and cash restrictions, raises penalties tied to stolen-metal transactions, prohibits specified copper cash purchases, and preserves existing municipal ordinances.

Builds procedures and advisory capacity for secure electronic voting by overseas voters while requiring an overseas-voter certificate, principally expanding remote ballot access with verification controls.

Creates an alternative commercial bird-hunting-preserve license where a regular hunting license is unnecessary and revises fees and requirements. It modifies regulated private hunting access without a clear broad ideological direction.
Raises the utility-gross-income threshold for reimbursement of highway-related relocation costs, expanding public cost sharing for smaller or mid-sized utilities.
Prohibits law-enforcement agencies from charging accident-response fees to motorists or insurers, reducing user charges and restricting agency fee authority.

Consolidates and revises oyster and seafood harvesting, management-station, sacking, fee, and penalty rules. It expands coordinated natural-resource and health regulation, though exact stringency requires text comparison.
Allows Class 7 municipalities to use alternate procedures to declare and abate overgrown-property nuisances. It is municipality-class-specific land-use enforcement.

The enrolled text creates a rebuttable presumption that a co-resident parent knows the child's best interest, bars visitation that endangers health or development, restricts claims after the related parent relinquishes custody or financially abandons the child, and expressly requires domestic-violence protections. It strengthens parental primacy while retaining individualized child-safety review.
Mandates ignition-interlock devices for specified DUI cases, creates restricted licensing and fees, and provides terms for indigent defendants, strengthening preventive alcohol-driving enforcement.
Authorizes state and local mutual-aid agreements with federally recognized tribes, expanding intergovernmental emergency-management cooperation and tribal inclusion.

Shortens the state's repurchase window when conveyed land is later privatized and exempts municipal commercial-development authorities from state-property transfer procedures, weakening public-asset safeguards to increase development flexibility.
Reimburses presidential-primary expenses in counties with Mardi Gras holiday accommodations. It is geographically specific election administration.

Requires replacement hunting acreage when state-owned or managed hunting land closes and mandates annual reporting, prioritizing continued public hunting access rather than general habitat conservation.
Omits domestic-violence victims' residential addresses from the statewide voter list, protecting survivor safety through a narrow public-record privacy exception.
Expands or restructures the Women's Commission's duties, staffing, benefits, funding, and fee authority, increasing institutional capacity for women-focused state policy.
Creates additional distinctive license-tag categories for current and former military members. It is primarily commemorative recognition.
Allows Etowah County elected officials to join the Employees' Retirement System instead of the supernumerary program. It is local compensation and pension administration.

Allows Etowah County sales-tax proceeds otherwise directed to capital projects to pay certified school and community-college personnel during proration. It is local education finance and earmark flexibility.
Requires Jefferson County to notify property owners of delinquent sewer bills within 90 days and makes unnotified bills uncollectible, creating a local utility consumer-protection rule.

Extends tax-increment financing to underused military-base lease areas, dedicating future incremental tax revenue to development. It expands targeted public financing of private or mixed-use redevelopment.
Revises Health Department regulation of emergency medical services and creates an advanced-EMT license category, modernizing professional and service oversight.
Expands dealer protections, manufacturer buyback duties, and compensation when a vehicle line is discontinued, regulating franchise relationships in favor of local dealers over manufacturers.

Authorizes judicial circuits, with district-attorney consent, to create drug courts offering screening, treatment, support, testing, and referrals. It expands a supervised treatment alternative to conventional prosecution or incarceration.
Renames a regional rapid-rail commission without changing powers or funding in the synopsis.
Prohibits texting or operating a handheld GPS while driving and imposes penalties, expanding road-safety regulation of personal device use.
Allows retirement boards to calculate accrued-liability contributions over 30 years, reducing near-term contribution pressure while extending pension financing obligations.
Reopens eligibility to purchase retirement service credit for prior federal Farm Service Agency work, expanding a defined public-pension benefit opportunity.
Creates a civil cause of action against convicted drug dealers for an individual's death, adding private liability to criminal drug enforcement.
Regulates rock-quarry locations near schools in unincorporated Madison County. It is a local land-use and environmental-health restriction.
Raises some court costs while lowering filing fees and directs added revenue to the Supreme Court Law Library. Its access-to-justice incidence is mixed without the fee schedule.
Gives priority to the person designated on a service member's federal emergency-data form for funeral decisions, harmonizing state law with a documented military designation.
Adds utility workers to the classes whose assault qualifies as second-degree assault, increasing punishment and occupational protection.
Exempts specified equipment purchased for commercial fishing vessels from sales and use tax, creating a targeted industry tax preference.

Requires immediate certificate revocation and termination after specified felony or child-sex-offense convictions, prioritizing student safety while eliminating ordinary tenure or dismissal protections for covered employees.
Appropriates funds to children's advocacy centers and requires operational plans, audits, and periodic reports, combining victim-service support with fiscal oversight.
Creates a state Trails Commission and advisory board to promote the Alabama Trails System, expanding public recreational and tourism planning capacity.

Bars municipalities outside Blount County from regulating or providing routine police and fire services in their Blount County police jurisdictions, except mutual aid. It is a local jurisdictional-control dispute.
Creates crimes and penalties for school employees' sexual acts or contact with students, expanding criminal protection against abuse of institutional authority.
Clarifies registration proof of federal heavy-vehicle tax payment and removes obsolete weight and deadline provisions. It is tax-compliance administration rather than a change in tax incidence.

Allows lifecycle costs in responsible-bid decisions and permits local governments to buy through existing federal contracts without a second bid, favoring long-run value and cooperative procurement over strict duplicative bidding.
Creates a temporary task force to assess Alzheimer's disease impacts and report recommendations. A study body alone does not establish a substantive spending or regulatory position.
Creates a nonresident pier-fishing license and adjusts license expiration dates. It is recreational-license administration without a clear broad ideological direction.
Alters Monroeville's corporate limits. Geometry and local context are required to infer representational or fiscal effects.
Authorizes a Monroe County sales-and-use tax and allocates revenue from most newly annexed Monroeville property to the county. It is local tax and intergovernmental revenue policy.
Alters Monroeville's corporate limits. Geometry and local context are required to infer representational or fiscal effects.
Further provides for membership of the Physical Therapy Board. The synopsis does not establish a directional licensing or scope-of-practice change.
Treats Corridor X/I-22 as an interstate for maximum-speed purposes, allowing the interstate speed regime on that corridor.
Allows Montgomery to establish an entertainment district where alcohol may be consumed throughout the district under conditions, locally liberalizing alcohol rules.
Criminalizes tampering with timber scales and broadens misdemeanor coverage for unauthorized timber transactions while exempting specified utility work, strengthening forest-property enforcement.
Protects a deployed military parent's custody and visitation rights from being treated as waived solely because of out-of-state service.
Revises Baldwin County personnel-appeal elections and contract-employee evaluation. It is local public-workforce administration.
Abolishes the office of constable in Blount County, a local governmental restructuring decision.
Creates a generally available POW/MIA license plate with an added fee supporting the Veterans' Assistance Fund. It combines commemoration with a small voluntary veterans benefit.
Allows an alternative teacher-unit calculation in exceptional circumstances with superintendent approval, providing flexibility that may preserve staffing where the standard formula misfits.

Redistributes TVA payments and liquor-tax increases among served and dry jurisdictions. It is regional revenue equalization whose winners and losers require fiscal detail, not a clean tax-ideology signal.
Removes plastic-tag and owner-license-number requirements from fur-bearing-animal traps, reducing accountability regulation on trapping.
Creates an additional Marshall County circuit judgeship conditioned on county financing, a local court-capacity measure.
Revises license tags and fees for government and volunteer fire vehicles. It is vehicle-registration administration.
Tightens graduated-license supervision and passenger or driving restrictions and prohibits handheld-device use by young drivers, expanding youth road-safety regulation.
Allows School Superintendents of Alabama officers and employees to continue participating in the Teachers' Retirement System, preserving a defined pension eligibility category.
Allows Auburn University's board to meet by teleconference or videoconference, a meeting-administration modernization without clear ideological direction.

Creates a Transportation Commission with appointment authority over the department director and revises department statutes, shifting transportation governance from the prior executive structure toward a commission model.
Allows honorably discharged Vietnam veterans whose service interrupted schooling to receive high-school diplomas. It is a narrow restorative and honorary educational benefit.

Revises mining commission schedules, licenses and fees, permits contract attorneys as hearing officers, and removes a hearing-attendance citation requirement after cessation orders. The package mixes administrative flexibility with a narrower enforcement procedure.
Creates licensing and safety rules for low-speed vehicles and mini-trucks while exempting them from titles, expanding lawful road access under tailored regulation.
Requires public notice of vacancies for state, local, and postsecondary education chief executives, strengthening hiring transparency.

Creates a publicly funded energy research and development grant program, commission, fund, appropriation, and legislative advisory role, expanding state investment in energy innovation without choosing a particular technology in the synopsis.
Exempts a named community health center from state and local sales and use tax, creating a targeted tax expenditure in support of nonprofit primary care.
Expresses support for the federal Jobs for Main Street Act, signaling support for recession-era federal employment and stimulus policy but changing no Alabama law.

Calls a specially elected constitutional convention to revise Alabama's 1901 Constitution and submits the result for voter ratification, supporting broad institutional reform through popular participation.
Urges a private athletic association to extend middle-school baseball season dates. It is a nonbinding, narrow extracurricular request.
Urges Congress and President Obama to enact clean-energy and climate legislation, a clear pro-climate-policy statement without direct state-law effect.
Requires restaurants and suppliers to disclose whether fish are domestic or imported beyond federal labeling rules, strengthening consumer-origin disclosure and scrutiny of imported seafood.
Extends second-degree-assault protection to off-duty law-enforcement officers working for private entities, expanding enhanced penalties and the protected reach of police status.
Raises allowable truck weight for functioning auxiliary-power or idle-reduction equipment, removing a regulatory disincentive to fuel-saving technology.
Removes an accreditation-progress condition and adds a qualifying Montgomery County institution to the student-grant program, broadening public aid eligibility at a targeted institution.
Allows public retirement boards to amortize accrued liabilities over 30 years, reducing near-term contributions while extending financing obligations.

Creates a voluntary annuity, disability, and death-benefit fund for paid and volunteer firefighters, financed by participant payments collected with property taxes and administered with public oversight.
Bars legislators from simultaneous employment in other state branches, agencies, or public education, with enforcement and liability, strengthening separation-of-powers and anti-double-dipping rules.
Removes requirements that a domestic insurer maintaining its home office elsewhere keep duplicate Alabama records and an officer-managed local office, while preserving commissioner access to records.

Creates procedures for transferring estate, trust, guardianship, and conservatorship cases between probate and circuit court. It is judicial administration without a clear substantive ideological direction.
Transfers elevator-safety fee revenue above the board's appropriation to the General Fund, weakening a dedicated regulatory-fee earmark in favor of general-budget flexibility.
Renames the Home Medical Equipment Board and revises its duties. The synopsis does not establish whether provider regulation expands or contracts.
Allows donated leave across pay grades and removes the hours cap for catastrophic, sick, or maternity leave, expanding a public-employee mutual-benefit program.

Modernizes state energy and residential codes and requires local implementation while exempting specified farm structures and prohibiting sprinkler mandates in certain homes. It combines energy regulation with limits on safety-code stringency.
Requires certificate revocation or termination for educators convicted of specified felonies or child-sex offenses, prioritizing student safety while narrowing tenure and dismissal protections.
Criminalizes leaving a child unattended in a vehicle and scales penalties by recurrence and injury, expanding child-safety criminal enforcement.
Further provides for membership of the Physical Therapy Board. The synopsis does not establish a directional licensing or scope-of-practice change.

Revises the Land Bank Authority's acquisition definition, voting, immunity, and redemption treatment for tax-delinquent property, facilitating public land-bank redevelopment with protections for governance and redemption.
Legalizes mixed martial arts under an expanded Athletic Commission and accompanying licensing and penalties, combining market liberalization with formal safety regulation.
Allows brewpubs to sell their beer to licensed wholesalers for retail distribution, liberalizing a constrained alcohol-production market within the three-tier system.
Redistributes Chambers County tobacco-tax revenue to a school, water infrastructure, and scholarships while abolishing a delegation service office. It is local earmark and institutional policy.

Requires Etowah County school-board election from single-member districts outside Attalla and Gadsden and authorizes a local committee to draw them. Representational effects require demographic and map review.
Creates a temporary Creek War and War of 1812 bicentennial commission. It is primarily historical commemoration.
Bars municipalities outside Blount County from regulating or routinely serving their Blount County police jurisdictions, except mutual aid. It is a local jurisdictional-control dispute.
Exempts nonclinical religious treatment from Mental Health Department licensure, expanding religious autonomy while removing ordinary provider safeguards for the exempt activity.
Charges applicants for interstate adult-offender supervision transfers and dedicates proceeds to probation upkeep, shifting supervision costs toward affected offenders.
Levies an additional Clay County tobacco tax, directs part to water feeder lines, and abolishes a delegation service office. It is local excise-tax and infrastructure policy.
Allows license revocation for youthful offenders whose underlying offense was manslaughter or vehicular homicide, expanding collateral punishment for serious driving deaths.
Increases Talladega County registrar meeting days, locally expanding voter-registration administrative availability.
Creates an alternate referendum procedure for Class 7 municipalities to adopt council-manager government. It is local institutional choice rather than a stable ideological signal.
Revises pharmacy and permit definitions within the licensing code. The synopsis does not establish a directional scope-of-practice or market-entry change.
Restricts multiple sex offenders from sharing residences or, under specified conditions, apartment complexes and adds civil penalties, expanding punitive housing exclusion.

Constitutionally authorizes bingo under a state commission, taxes and licenses the activity, subjects regulators to ethics and open-meeting laws, and restricts specified campaign contributions. It combines gambling liberalization with strong public regulation.
Creates a POW/MIA license plate for any resident with a voluntary additional fee supporting veterans assistance.
Revises Dental Board fees and quorum rules. Without amounts or changed powers, ideological direction is not established.
Revises the Women's Commission's qualifications, duties, funding, and terms, strengthening or restructuring women-focused state capacity; exact fiscal expansion requires text.

The engrossed text adds a time-limited pathway allowing holders of an approved engineering bachelor's degree, an engineering doctorate, four years of progressive experience, and a passed practice examination to obtain licensure. It expands eligibility for a highly credentialed applicant class while retaining examination and experience requirements.

Revises eligibility proof and residency rules and directs development of contingent-funding criteria for disabled-veteran education benefits, supporting administered access subject to available funds.
Creates a conditional early-retirement incentive for Jefferson County employees, a local workforce and pension-management measure.
Allows removal of municipal officials for specified missed meetings while protecting military absences and permitting reinstatement, strengthening attendance accountability with a service exception.

The engrossed text moves the legacy exemption test from 20 years of operation as of April 1980 to 20 years as of January 2004, extending exemption to a newer cohort of accredited Alabama private schools. It reduces state licensing coverage while retaining recognized accreditation and loss-of-accreditation safeguards.
Creates a Mobile-specific procedure to quiet title to tax-sale property acquired from the state, facilitating reuse or disposition of delinquent property.
Requires advance notice, fiscal analysis, and majority committee action before Jefferson County revenue measures, strengthening local tax-process safeguards.
Authorizes drug courts with screening, treatment, support services, testing, and referrals and provides civil immunity, expanding a supervised treatment alternative to conventional punishment.
Protects otherwise lawful contracts to buy or sell lots in proposed subdivisions from impairment by municipal subdivision regulation, prioritizing contract and development rights.
Authorizes district attorneys to appoint investigators with law-enforcement powers, expanding prosecutorial policing capacity.
Bars municipalities outside Blount County from regulating or routinely serving their Blount County police jurisdictions, except mutual aid. It is a local jurisdictional-control dispute.
Requires DeKalb County to hold special elections for specified county-office vacancies, favoring direct electoral selection over extended appointment.
Requires Jackson County to hold special elections for specified county-office vacancies, favoring direct electoral selection over extended appointment.
Allows the Franklin County district attorney to employ investigators with arrest powers, locally expanding prosecutorial policing capacity.
Allows officers and employees of the Alabama Higher Education Partnership to participate in the Teachers' Retirement System, expanding eligibility beyond conventional public education employment.
Requires special elections for specified Perry County constitutional-office vacancies, favoring direct electoral selection over extended appointment.
Alters Fort Payne's corporate limits. Geometry and local context are required to infer representational or fiscal effects.
Protects confidentiality of counseling-board complaint and investigation files while correcting code references, prioritizing investigatory privacy over public disclosure.
Merges Prichard's water and sewer board into the Mobile regional system with transfer of assets and debt. It is local public-utility consolidation.
Creates a breast-cancer-research license plate whose added voluntary fee funds the state research foundation.

The proposed amendment replaces detailed 1901 corporate rules with general-law authority, retains legislative regulation and business-privilege taxation, and restates shareholder limited liability. It repeals charter, foreign-corporation, securities, railroad-rate, free-pass, and related constitutional safeguards, making this principally constitutional corporate deregulation and modernization rather than wholesale withdrawal of legislative power.
Extends the rebuttable presumption against a child's change of principal residence to initial custody decisions, prioritizing geographic stability in family-court adjudication.
Allows Limestone County to use existing sales-tax proceeds to refinance bonds. It is local debt-management flexibility.
Adds Lawrence County court costs to drug cases and directs revenue to drug-law enforcement, locally expanding punitive user-financed enforcement.
Establishes subsidized kinship guardianship and legal procedures, supporting children remaining with extended family rather than formal foster placement.

The introduced text authorizes medical regulators to charge a physician found in violation for independent review, experts, outside counsel, attorney fees, depositions, staff travel, evidence, and other prescribed expenses, enforceable like a fine. It also routes review of controlled-substance registration suspension or revocation to the Court of Civil Appeals, materially strengthening board cost-recovery and enforcement leverage.
Allows Geneva County fire districts and service fees after referendum and provides governance and dissolution rules. It is local public-safety finance.
Adds Etowah County court costs and a solicitor's fee to fund prosecution. It is local criminal-justice finance.
Revises Randolph County tobacco-tax collection and distribution and abolishes a delegation service office. It is local fiscal administration.
Exempts farm-raised yellow perch from a fish-sale prohibition, liberalizing aquaculture commerce while leaving wild-resource restrictions intact.

Revises removal and participation bans for bank insiders, change-of-control review, board procedure, and interstate acquisitions. It modernizes prudential supervision, but individual deregulatory or restrictive effects require text.
Includes State Banking Department licensees within the used-motor-vehicle dealer definition, extending or clarifying dealer licensing coverage.
Creates a temporary task force to assess Alzheimer's impacts and recommend policy. A study body alone does not establish a substantive spending or regulatory position.

Allows people outside Alabama on military or mission assignments to declare state residency for general purposes while expressly excluding election eligibility, protecting non-electoral domicile ties.
Allows Elmore County's sheriff to contract for service of process and charges fees on served documents for the sheriff's fund. It is local justice-service financing and contracting.
Alters Stevenson's corporate limits. Geometry and local context are required to infer representational or fiscal effects.
Revises proof-of-insurance and reinstatement-fee procedures for mandatory liability coverage, strengthening or streamlining enforcement while imposing costs on noncompliant drivers.

Allows large municipalities to create entertainment districts with broader alcohol consumption, subject to ABC licensing, local regulation, and fees. It liberalizes alcohol access within a regulated framework.
Makes Marshall County circuit and district judicial elections nonpartisan, removing party labels from a local elected judiciary.
Prohibits smoking in restaurants, expanding indoor-air public-health regulation while limiting proprietor and patron discretion.
Alters Hayden's corporate limits. Geometry and local context are required to infer representational or fiscal effects.

Broadens criminal-history exchange and licensing background checks, creates a statistical-analysis center, and criminalizes misuse of justice information. It expands surveillance capacity with a data-abuse safeguard.
Adds Franklin County criminal court costs to finance a courthouse and jail, shifting local justice infrastructure costs toward defendants.
Distributes Morgan County TVA payments to local school boards for FY2010 and FY2011. It is temporary local public-education finance.
Repeals a requirement that Perry County provide three specified probate-court clerks. It is local staffing flexibility and potential capacity reduction.

The enrolled act requires a special election within 60 to 90 days whenever a Perry County commission vacancy has at least 12 months remaining, with the winner serving the balance of the term. It locally favors direct popular selection over appointment.
Alters Piedmont's corporate limits. Geometry and local context are required to infer representational or fiscal effects.
Requires special elections for specified Lowndes County constitutional-office vacancies, favoring direct electoral selection over extended appointment.
Authorizes automated red-light cameras and civil fines in Center Point with signage, records, appeals, and anti-tampering rules. It is local surveillance-based traffic enforcement.

Continues the Court Reporting Board, revises appointments, requires continuing education, limits board liability, and creates a temporary graduate license. It maintains professional regulation while adding an entry pathway.
Adds salvia divinorum and Salvinorin A to Schedule I, subjecting them to the state's strictest controlled-substance prohibitions.
Revises distribution of additional TVA payments in Limestone County. It is local intergovernmental revenue allocation.
Requires special elections for specified Greene County constitutional-office vacancies, favoring direct electoral selection over extended appointment.
Revises membership, terms, and officers of the Music Hall of Fame Board. It is cultural-institution administration.
Converts Washington County commissioner expense allowances into salary. It is local compensation administration.
Authorizes Washington County commission contingent-fund appropriations and expenditures. It is local budget authority without a specified policy direction.
Establishes an audited Autauga County sheriff work-release program, locally expanding a structured alternative to full custodial confinement.
Allows a passport as proof of identity and age for a learner's license, expanding accepted documentation.
Commends a named state senator. It contains no substantive policy position.
Renames an Alabama State University complex. It is ceremonial institutional naming.

The enrolled resolution confirms that the Legislature overrode the governor to sustain committee disapproval of a Personnel Board layoff-rule amendment, but it does not reproduce or characterize that amendment. Legislative oversight clearly increases; the effect on employee layoff protection remains unknowable without the January 2009 Administrative Monthly rule text.

The enrolled resolution rejects the Board of Education's rule as ambiguous and unenforceable, supports a committee-written code expressly defining unethical conduct and disciplinary sanctions, and overrides the governor's veto. It clearly favors tougher, more enforceable teacher ethics rules and stronger legislative control over agency rulemaking.
