Authorizes and retroactively validates a Greene County sheriff-operated jail store whose proceeds fund law enforcement, subject to audit. It is local carceral enterprise finance.

Prohibits texting or operating handheld wireless devices while driving, imposes penalties, and requires law-enforcement statistical reporting, expanding road-safety regulation with an enforcement-monitoring requirement.

Narrows protected underwater cultural resources to shipwreck-associated items and authorizes recovery of other abandoned artifacts in specified places, expanding private salvage at the expense of broader public archaeological protection.
Excludes the towed vehicle from wreckers' gross-weight licensing and registration calculation, reducing the regulatory or fee burden on tow-truck operators.

Allows the Pharmacy Board to regulate repackaging and storage of noncontrolled prescription drugs for nursing-home and assisted-living residents, enabling medication reuse or redistribution under professional rules.

Extends state death and disability benefits to all law-enforcement officers and treats cancer, AIDS, and hepatitis as occupational diseases, substantially expanding public safety employee protections.

Creates exceptions to a telephone carrier's last-resort service obligation when property owners or developers arrange alternative service, expanding private contracting while narrowing universal-service duties.
Expedites seizure and disposition of fighting dogs, requires bonds in specified cases, and expands forfeiture, strengthening animal-welfare enforcement through punitive property procedures.

Continues security-industry licensing while requiring board members to be Alabama citizens and applicants to be U.S. citizens or legally present, adding immigration-status restrictions to occupational entry.
Allows officers with reasonable suspicion of unlicensed driving to demand a license and issue a citation, expanding investigatory police authority for licensing enforcement.

The introduced text lets municipalities publish only a specified synopsis of planning, zoning, and business-licensing ordinances instead of the full text, while requiring a full copy from the clerk and 30-day web posting where a municipal website exists. It trades reduced newspaper detail and cost for standardized summaries and conditional online access.
Enacts the annual public-education budget. Ideological direction requires amounts and changes relative to prior funding, not merely the existence of appropriations.
Constitutionally prohibits counties and municipalities from levying occupational taxes, restricting local revenue authority and establishing an anti-tax rule.
Extends or clarifies immunity for sheriff's employees, reducing civil-liability exposure for local law-enforcement personnel.
Extends payments into the Forever Wild Land Trust for 20 years, preserving long-term public conservation funding.

Extends the coal excise and privilege tax rather than allowing it to expire and revises distribution of its proceeds. This preserves an industry-specific tax and public revenue stream and should not be collapsed into a generic tax-burden score.

Allows life-cycle costs in responsible-bid selection and permits local governments to use vendors holding federal GSA contracts without another competitive bid. It combines broader value assessment with a defined relaxation of duplicative bidding.

Shortens the statute of repose protecting architects, engineers, and builders, increasing the period-relative ability of injured plaintiffs to maintain covered civil actions and expanding professional liability exposure.
Bars youthful-offender status for charges involving intentional serious physical injury or death, moving covered young defendants toward ordinary adult punishment.
Retroactively validates specified municipal annexations under defined conditions. This resolves local boundary legality without a stable statewide ideological direction.

Requires a state financial-capacity determination and raises the population threshold before most municipalities may establish a city school system. It constrains municipal fragmentation and expands state gatekeeping over local education governance.
Prohibits counties operating sewer systems from charging people or entities not connected to the system, establishing a targeted ratepayer and property-owner protection.
Abolishes the constable office in Marengo County. This is a local governmental-structure decision without a generalizable ideological direction.
Continues a Hale County ad valorem tax initially authorized for a jail and directs excess receipts to law enforcement. The tax incidence and spending are clear but locally specific.

Requires Jefferson County to employ a qualified county manager in an at-will non-merit position. The measure is a local governance and personnel restructuring rather than a broadly comparable policy vote.
Revises the procedure for filling mayoral vacancies in municipalities above a population threshold. The synopsis supplies no durable ideological conflict.

Moves specified Jefferson County positions from classified civil service to at-will status while addressing return rights, compensation, and benefits. The primary direction weakens merit-system job protection.

Expands and clarifies county planning authority over subdivisions in municipal extraterritorial jurisdictions and permits intergovernmental agreements. This is greater land-use regulation paired with jurisdictional coordination.

Grants property owners limited civil immunity for good-faith defense of self, others, or property against a person unlawfully present and engaged in criminal conduct, subject to exceptions. It expands defensive legal protection.
Raises the income threshold triggering statements of economic interests and exempts additional employees, reducing the reach of state ethics disclosure requirements.
Authorizes large and mid-sized municipalities to establish regulated entertainment districts permitting alcohol sales and consumption. This liberalizes alcohol rules within designated local areas.
Expands the required distance between funeral protests and funeral-property lines. It protects mourners and public order by imposing a greater spatial restriction on protest speech.
Repeals specified investigation provisions under Anniston's council-manager charter. The local institutional change lacks a stable statewide ideological direction from the synopsis.

Creates a process to determine whether secure electronic voting can serve overseas voters and directs implementation if appropriate. It seeks expanded military and overseas access while expressly retaining a security assessment.
Extends residential-property classification to qualifying single-family dwellings and lots under construction, broadening access to the preferential residential ad valorem treatment.
Caps asbestos damages against successor corporations at the acquired entity's pre-merger or consolidation asset value, limiting tort recovery and corporate successor liability.
Authorizes the Governor and local emergency agencies to enter mutual-aid agreements with federally recognized tribes, expanding intergovernmental emergency cooperation.
Prohibits private obligations imposing fees on future real-property transfers and supplies enforcement rules, restricting long-lived private encumbrances on ownership and alienation.
Increases Escambia County's service-of-process fee and earmarks it for law enforcement. It is a localized user-fee and agency-funding decision.

Creates an Agriculture Department approval and fee process for agricultural tourist attractions and allows qualifying directional signs. The bill supports rural tourism while adding a modest certification regime.

Makes licensing examinations board-approved, removes the $300 examination-fee cap, and replaces fixed three-member rules for discipline and revoked-license reissuance with a majority of deliberating members while defining a simple-majority quorum. It expands board and fee flexibility and changes governance thresholds without a single regulatory scalar.
Adds a Marengo County property-instrument recording fee for the probate office. This is a local user-fee and office-funding measure.
Extends the special unemployment-compensation assessment financing the Employment Security Enhancement Fund, retaining an employer-side charge and dedicated program funding.
Creates a comprehensive Insurance Department licensing and regulatory regime for insurance adjusters, expanding occupational oversight of the industry.

Revises administration and authorized use of Elevator Safety Review Board funds within the Labor Department. The synopsis shows an agency-accounting change but no clear shift in safety standards or regulated-party burdens.
Authorizes a special filing fee in Marengo County probate court. This is a local court-finance measure.

Replaces the wireless-focused board with a statewide 911 board, centralizes collection of a service charge, and distributes proceeds to local enhanced-911 districts. It expands coordinated public-safety infrastructure financed through a user charge.
Creates procedures for consumers to place, lift, and remove credit-report security freezes with notices, fees, and enforcement, expanding identity-theft and financial-privacy protections.

Raises the education prerequisite from high school to completion of a court-reporting program, broadens permissible exam administrators, and authorizes new processing and information-change fees, while eliminating board-member compensation and annual executive reporting. The package tightens entry qualifications and fees but reduces administrative reporting.
Revises provider licensure while adding disciplinary hearings, administrative fines, injunctions, and penalties, strengthening enforcement of home-medical-equipment regulation.
Allows additional nonprofit schools to seek exemption from state licensure, reducing regulation for qualifying nonprofit education providers.

Continues and expands Athletic Commission regulation to amateur and professional mixed martial arts while limiting licensure to citizens or people legally present. It combines safety and occupational regulation with an immigration-status eligibility restriction.

Exempts qualifying volunteer fire departments, rescue squads, associations, and local fire districts from sales, use, and ad valorem taxes, providing targeted fiscal support to emergency-service organizations.
Allows University of South Alabama trustees to participate in meetings by telephone or video under specified conditions, modernizing board access without changing substantive university policy.

Revises bait-shrimp areas, basket limits, minnow traps, license duration, and fees. The measure mixes resource-management liberalization and restrictions with a higher license charge and should not receive one scalar environmental or tax label.
Authorizes local warning signs on residential roads for children who are deaf or blind, supporting disability safety accommodation.
Continues the Sickle Cell Oversight and Regulatory Commission through its next sunset date without describing a substantive policy change.

Creates territorial, termination, inventory-repurchase, and warranty rules governing recreational-vehicle manufacturer and dealer agreements, expanding statutory protection for dealers and constraining manufacturers.

Creates a rebuttable presumption that the parent with whom a child lives knows the child's best interest and bars harmful visitation, strengthening parental-rights and child-safety limits. It also adds petition grounds when a parent relinquishes custody or financially abandons the child, so the bill is not purely restrictive of grandparent claims.
Establishes a state housing trust fund and advisory committee to support housing opportunities for low- and moderate-income households, expanding public affordable-housing infrastructure.
Creates a commission to implement streamlined multistate sales-and-use-tax compliance, strengthening tax-administration capacity rather than changing the statutory rate.
Provides a vehicle allowance for the Lee County coroner. This is local officer compensation.
Abolishes the constable office in Lee County, a local governmental-structure decision.
Continues the General Contractors Licensing Board under sunset review with modifications not described in the synopsis. No reliable ideological direction is stated.

Mandates ignition-interlock use and restricted licenses for covered DUI cases while including provisions for indigent defendants. It expands punitive and preventive supervision with an ability-to-pay safeguard.
Requires Internet retailers to notify Alabama purchasers of use-tax obligations and authorizes income-tax-form collection mechanisms, strengthening compliance with existing sales and use taxes.

Places the gun-show business-license tax on the organizer rather than individual participants under covered conditions. This consolidates tax incidence and administration without altering firearm possession rights.
Constitutionally provides for elected four-year Montgomery County school-board terms. It expands direct local electoral selection but is geographically specific.
Creates a Montgomery County authority to develop the Catoma Creek reservoir area. The local development-governance measure lacks enough fiscal detail for a broader subsidy judgment.
Exempts plumbing work performed by an owner on the owner's own property from board certification, reducing occupational-licensing reach for self-performed work.
Provides for countywide election of the Montgomery County superintendent with terms and qualifications. This is a local shift toward direct electoral control.
Increases funding for nursing scholarships and revises eligibility, expanding public support for health-workforce education.

Creates a comprehensive adult and juvenile sex-offender registration and notification regime, limits residence and employment, and authorizes fees. It substantially expands punitive supervision and community-notification policy.
Continues the professional board through its next sunset date without a stated substantive regulatory change.

Clarifies DHR screening of people with unsupervised access to vulnerable populations and permits prosecution, termination, or foster/adoptive denial for inadvertently false criminal-history information, while providing disqualifying reports to applicants and removing duplicative Education Department requests. It mixes broader punitive screening with notice and administrative-streamlining safeguards.

Authorizes or strengthens penalties for violating Forestry Commission rules governing conduct on state-forest land, expanding public-land rule enforcement. Exact penalty levels are not stated in the synopsis.

Reconstitutes massage-board representation across congressional districts and removes the requirement that qualifying education be accredited by the Education Department. It combines geographic governance requirements with reduced educational gatekeeping.
Continues Colbert County's solicitor fee while repealing superseded local acts. This is a local court-finance measure.
Makes willful deceptive removal or underreporting of uncompensated timber a Class A misdemeanor, expanding criminal protection for landowners and forest-product property.

Authorizes Forestry Commission timber sales from public land under specified conditions and exempts those sales from general surplus-property procedures. It permits resource disposition while relaxing ordinary sale safeguards.
Extends the unemployment-compensation benefit period, increasing income support for eligible unemployed workers.
Moves the registration blackout from 10 to 14 days before an election, closing registration four days earlier and restricting late voter access.

Authorizes Montgomery's automated speed-camera enforcement with civil fines, notice, court review, records, and signage. It expands surveillance-based traffic enforcement while providing procedural safeguards.

Authorizes targeted tax incentives for new, expanding, and retained companies and educational institutions subject to capital-investment and job requirements. It expands conditional industrial subsidies rather than broad-based tax relief.

Continues the bar admissions board while requiring applicants to be citizens or lawfully present and board members to be state citizens. The substantive direction is restrictive occupational eligibility based on immigration and residency status.
Expands property and construction-transaction tax abatements for qualifying data-processing centers, providing sector-specific development subsidies.

Creates the Garrett Coliseum Redevelopment Corporation with development powers and revenue-bond authority while reorganizing the Agricultural Center Board. It expands public redevelopment and debt-financing machinery.
Continues the athletic-trainer board, adds meeting notice, and clarifies annual license expiration. These are sunset and administrative-governance changes without a material ideological shift.
Allows the Lawrence County sheriff to give a retiring officer a badge and pistol. This is a local ceremonial and compensation-related measure rather than general gun policy.
Authorizes Winfield to establish and fund a board for its municipal theater. The cultural-governance measure is local.

Repeals the act establishing and funding the Twenty-fifth Judicial Circuit public-defender office. On the stated text this reduces a dedicated indigent-defense institution, though replacement arrangements are not described.
Allows Baldwin County's budget and information-systems directors to be hired as contract employees outside the ordinary merit-system structure, reducing civil-service coverage for those posts.
Creates an income-tax-refund checkoff for voluntary contributions to the state Historic Preservation Fund, facilitating privately directed conservation support without imposing a tax increase.
Removes the exemption of coal ash and related combustion byproducts from solid-waste regulation, expanding environmental oversight of fossil-fuel waste.
Creates an income-tax-refund checkoff for voluntary contributions to a veterinary spay-neuter program, facilitating animal-welfare funding without a compulsory tax.

Expands protected service-animal use in public places and schools to people with blindness, hearing impairment, and autism-spectrum diagnoses and authorizes training access, strengthening disability accommodation.
Establishes and funds an Insurance Department program to retrofit insurable homes against hurricane and wind losses, expanding public disaster-resilience support.
Increases punishment for a third or subsequent indecent-exposure conviction, expanding repeat-offender penalties under sexual-morality and public-order law.
Extends Good Samaritan civil immunity to uncompensated people participating in emergency response in good faith, reducing liability barriers to volunteer assistance.

Authorizes Center Point camera enforcement of red lights, stop signs, and speeding, backed by civil fines and a traffic-safety fund, while providing notice, hearings, and appeals. It expands automated public-order enforcement with procedural protections.

Adds covered conduct to domestic-violence offenses, increases repeat penalties, creates emergency-call-interference and strangulation offenses, and bars specified court costs for victims. It combines punitive expansion with victim access and protection measures.

Clarifies regulated treatment while exempting licensed professional counselors and churches or ministries providing religious services from Mental Health Department licensure. It reduces state regulation for professional and religious providers.

Allows public members or officers to retain a financial interest in specified contracts predating service or when they abstain from the decision, broadening exceptions to public-contract conflict rules.

Expands the Birmingham public-safety pension board's alternative-investment discretion, removes the rule placing at least half of fixed-income assets in federal securities, and removes an investment-grade rating requirement while adding mandatory federal tax provisions. This increases investment flexibility and risk tolerance rather than changing promised benefits.
Includes Roth IRAs within probate-law restrictions on assignment and alienation, expanding protection of retirement savings from transfer or creditor claims.

Extends prompt-payment protections to private construction retainage, caps withholding at five percent, stops further retainage after 50 percent completion, prevents contractors from withholding a greater percentage from lower tiers than owners withhold, and applies 12-percent annual interest to excess withholding. It strengthens payment protection for contractors and subcontractors.

Moves pesticide registration to a biennial cycle and creates a new fee schedule. This changes regulatory administration and regulated-party costs, but the synopsis does not state whether the annualized fee rises or falls.

Preempts local fertilizer ordinances and reserves the subject to the state Agriculture Department subject to an exception. It restricts local environmental authority through statewide agricultural preemption.
Allows presiding circuit judges to conduct specified civil hearings by audio-video communication, expanding remote court access and administrative flexibility.

Restructures Alabama A&M governance through a nominating committee and training program, permits an at-large trustee from outside Alabama, and expands board powers. This is institutional governance modernization without a simple partisan scalar.

Rewrites constitutional banking provisions to require general-law charters, allow unlimited duration, and prohibit political subdivisions from owning bank stock or lending credit. It favors standardized private banking and limits public ownership.

Rewrites Article XII to preserve general-law incorporation, a business privilege tax, and shareholder limited liability while repealing constitutional restrictions on corporate charters, stock and bond issuance, foreign corporations, railroad rebates, free passes, and related regulation. It is a broad constitutional corporate deregulation and modernization package with core tax and liability rules retained.
Creates licensure and road-use rules for low-speed vehicles and mini-trucks, requires safety equipment, and waives titles. It liberalizes use subject to safety regulation.
Extends second-degree assault treatment to attacks on off-duty officers performing lawful private employment, expanding enhanced criminal protection for law enforcement.
Creates a statewide Blue Alert system for suspects accused of injuring officers and missing officers, expanding law-enforcement emergency notification infrastructure.

Revises publication of port-authority bond notices and requires civil challenges within a defined period. The core effect is faster finality for public development debt and reduced time to contest issuance.
Revises board membership, terms, qualifications, diversity, and chair selection for a commemorative institution. It is governance rather than substantive policy.
Adds and revises first- and second-degree stalking and aggravated-stalking offenses, expanding criminal law addressing repeated threats and harassment.
Reopens the opportunity for public employees to purchase retirement credit for prior USDA Farm Service Agency work, expanding pension-credit access through employee purchase.
Creates a voluntary income-tax-refund checkoff supporting the Alabama Firefighters Annuity and Benefit Fund without imposing a compulsory tax.
Requires monthly General Fund and Education Trust Fund reports to be published online, expanding fiscal transparency.

Updates the prosthetics and orthotics licensing act, retains nationally grounded facility accreditation, revises practitioner categories and applications, expands board administration, and permits maximum fees to be exceeded under specified fiscal conditions. The measure generally strengthens and modernizes professional regulation while increasing potential regulated-party fees.
Limits the number and use of dealer plates while creating transit plates for covered movements, tightening misuse controls and supplying a narrower administrative alternative.

Broadly restructures Alabama's criminal-justice information center, expands data and homeland-security functions, criminalizes misuse, and joins a national crime-prevention and privacy compact. It expands state information capacity while adding privacy and misuse constraints.
Legalizes personal home production of beer, cider, and wine by adults without taxation or licensure, liberalizing alcohol and hobby-production rules.
Authorizes title insurers to offer closing or settlement insurance for settlement agents, expanding permissible private insurance products.
Alters Foley's municipal boundaries. This is a local annexation measure.
Adopts a statutory perpetuities rule allowing trusts to delay vesting for up to 360 years, expanding long-term private control of wealth and property beyond the ordinary 100-year period.
Alters Foley's municipal boundaries. This is local geography rather than ideological legislation.
Adds a Monroe County service-of-process fee for law-enforcement purposes. This is localized user-fee financing.
Allows online Monroe County property-tax payment with a transaction fee. This is a local service convenience and user charge.
Allows Internet and mail vehicle-tag renewal in Monroe County with convenience or mailing fees. This is local administrative access financed by user charges.
Adopts a uniform procedure recognizing unsworn declarations by people outside the United States, reducing formal barriers in civil practice while retaining statutory conditions.

Streamlines certificate-of-need contested cases, creates direct appellate review, and caps specified administrative-law costs. It reduces procedural delay and expense while retaining the underlying health-facility planning regime.
Provides and regulates subsidized-adoption payments with termination, reporting, and hearing procedures, strengthening public support and due process for covered adoptive families.

Reorganizes the Alabama Development Office as a Commerce Department and authorizes selected employment outside the Merit System, combining economic-development centralization with weaker civil-service coverage.
Raises the permitted late charge on specified consumer-credit transactions, shifting costs toward delinquent borrowers and expanding creditor fee authority.
Continues the wastewater board while restricting licensure to citizens or people lawfully present, adding an immigration-status barrier to occupational entry.
Proposes a voter-approved Dothan property-tax increase for public schools and the local library. The fiscal direction is clear but geographically specific.

Moves motor-fuel taxation upstream to terminal withdrawal and comprehensively replaces licensing, distribution, and penalty statutes. It centralizes tax administration and enforcement without a stated rate increase.
Continues athlete-agent regulation while limiting registration to citizens or lawfully present applicants, creating an immigration-status occupational restriction.
Deletes the prohibition on an alcohol licensee, agent, or employee working for another licensee, reducing industry employment regulation.

Requires write-in candidates to register before the election and comply with campaign-finance and ethics law and establishes counting procedures. It restricts unregistered write-in candidacies while regularizing disclosure and tabulation.
Continues the Historical Commission under sunset review without changing substantive preservation policy.
Makes a public appropriation to Lyman Ward Military Academy, providing targeted state support to a private educational institution.
Makes a state appropriation to Tuskegee University, providing targeted support to a historically Black educational institution.
Transfers Children First Trust Fund receipts allocated to the State Board of Education into the General Fund for the fiscal year, reducing the protected education and children's-program earmark.
Makes a state appropriation to Talladega College, providing targeted support to a historically Black educational institution.

Continues the landscape-architect board while requiring state citizenship for members and citizenship or lawful presence for license applicants, adding residency and immigration-status entry restrictions.
Exempts veterans with a 100-percent service-connected disability from distinctive-tag fees and vehicle ad valorem tax, expanding targeted veterans' tax relief.
Changes the presidential-primary date and removes a special Mardi Gras conflict rule. This is election scheduling without an evident partisan access direction from the synopsis.
Replaces the Revenue Department's internal Administrative Law Division with a Tax Appeals Commission and formal review procedures, increasing institutional separation in taxpayer adjudication.
Continues the professional engineer and land-surveyor board under sunset review without a stated substantive change.
Allows Jasper to authorize draft or keg beer sales, a local liberalization of alcohol rules.
Changes candidate qualifying dates in a specified municipal government form. The synopsis establishes election administration but no directional access effect.
Allows local boards to redirect child-nutrition funds to other current expenses with state approval for the fiscal year, weakening a protected school-meal earmark during budget stress.
Adopts market-based sourcing for sales of services and intangibles when apportioning multistate business income, shifting tax liability toward the customer's market rather than production location.
Requires proof of existing federal heavy-vehicle excise-tax payment for registration and removes obsolete provisions. It is tax-compliance administration rather than a new burden.
Replaces an advisory board with a Governor's Mansion Authority and transfers governance, funding, and staffing functions. This is institutional reorganization without a clear policy valence.
Allows Madison County to determine dangerous-dog status, require fenced confinement, and impose civil penalties in unincorporated areas, expanding local public-safety and animal-control regulation.
Continues the architect registration board under sunset review without a stated substantive regulatory change.
Shortens deadlines for courts and the Public Safety Department to report traffic convictions, strengthening interstate and commercial-driver enforcement information.
Authorizes Midfield camera enforcement of red lights with civil fines, records, appeals, and anti-tampering penalties. It expands automated traffic enforcement while providing procedural review.
Exempts parts and supplies used to refurbish large commercial aircraft from sales tax, providing a targeted tax preference to the aviation industry.

Continues the polygraph board, expands its authority to set consultant qualifications, and restricts licensure to citizens or lawfully present applicants. It combines professional gatekeeping with an immigration-status barrier.

Comprehensively expands and modernizes dental regulation, including whitening, mobile operations, nonprofit clinics, sedation training and informed consent, record duties, discipline, and higher fines and fees, while deleting a minimum fee schedule and adding some teaching and reapplication pathways. It strengthens consumer-safety and professional oversight but also removes price-floor regulation.
Allows electronic filing of Shelby County business personal-property returns, a local administrative modernization.
Deletes the rule limiting how many Senior Services board members may share one faith, reducing a religious-composition constraint on public appointments.
Extends the time to fill a local superintendent vacancy and authorizes an interim appointment. This is administrative continuity rather than ideological education policy.
Allows Athens to authorize and regulate draft or keg beer sales, a local alcohol liberalization.
Continues the occupational-therapy board while imposing state-citizenship rules on members and citizenship or lawful-presence rules on applicants, adding residency and immigration-status barriers.

Expands Attorney General staffing, opinion, subpoena, and prosecution authority; permits more non-merit appointments and out-of-state deputies; removes legislative contract review; caps retained recoveries at actual office expenses; and creates a false-statement crime for investigations. It centralizes executive legal power while adding a fiscal cap and employment restrictions on private practice.
Authorizes the University of South Alabama president to employ police officers and defines their duties, expanding campus law-enforcement capacity.

Extends unsafe-and-unsound-practice orders, civil penalties, and officer removal to bank holding companies, protects supervisory proceedings and reports as confidential, and requires notice of ownership changes through inheritance. It strengthens prudential oversight while limiting public disclosure of supervisory information.

Requires a public hearing when census growth would change a municipality's government form and allows 10 percent of voters to trigger a referendum, while clarifying mayoral appointment authority and preserving council review and requested due process for removals. It expands local democratic control and procedural protection.
Adds a Clarke County solicitor fee supporting the circuit clerk and district attorney. This is localized court financing.
Adds court costs in Elmore County for the clerk and judicial complex. This is localized user-fee financing.
Raises Clarke County's lodging tax, a geographically specific consumption-tax increase.
Allows the Conecuh school board to insure property through either the State Insurance Fund or a private insurer. This is local procurement flexibility.
Revises Macon County commission duties over roads without stating the operative allocation. It is local governance.
Provides no-cost distinctive license tags to Legion of Valor members, expanding targeted veterans' fee relief.
Authorizes additional Cleburne County court costs in traffic cases. This is a local defendant fee.
Directs a portion of Marshall County TVA payments to local school boards. This is local education-funding allocation.
Redraws State Board of Education districts following the 2010 census. Without evidence of representational effect, this is mandatory redistricting administration.
Allows an existing Etowah sales-tax capital allocation to support certified school and community-college personnel during proration. This is local budget flexibility protecting education staffing.
Allows Madison County to regulate alcohol licenses and impose a privilege or license fee. This is local alcohol administration and revenue.
Alters Gulf Shores' municipal boundaries. This is local geography.
Authorizes transfer of school-trust lands and income to the Cullman County school board. This is local education-asset governance.
Allows Sunday alcohol sales in specified Tuscaloosa County territory subject to voter approval, a local liberalization with referendum control.
Creates a Coffee County work-release fund for law enforcement subject to audit. This is local criminal-justice financing.
Alters Killen's municipal boundaries. This is local geography.
Revises commission responsibility for roads, compensation, and employment of a county engineer while repealing local acts. This is local administrative structure.
Revises a Montgomery County recording fee and directs it to probate record-system improvements. This is local user-fee financing.
Establishes a Tuscaloosa pretrial-diversion program, expanding alternatives to conventional prosecution for eligible defendants.

Constitutionally guarantees secret ballots for public votes and employee-representation decisions. Applied to labor organizing, it blocks recognition methods such as voluntary card check and favors election-based union certification.
Changes distribution of Jefferson County lodging-tax proceeds to the general fund subject to exceptions. This is local revenue allocation.
Omits protected domestic-violence victims' residential addresses from the statewide voter list, strengthening survivor privacy without limiting their registration.
Authorizes a Jefferson County occupational tax subject to voter approval. It is a local earned-income tax and revenue measure.
Alters Gulf Shores' municipal boundaries. This is local geography.
Establishes a pretrial-diversion program in the Sixteenth Judicial Circuit, expanding alternatives to prosecution for eligible defendants.
Changes distribution of an existing Jefferson County sales tax to the general fund subject to exceptions. This is local revenue allocation.
Sets meeting hours for the Birmingham school board. This is local administrative procedure.
Allows Sunday alcohol sales in Northport subject to voter approval, a local liberalization with referendum control.
Adds Tuscaloosa County court costs for clerks and the law library. This is localized court financing.
Revises a Madison County municipal-court fee supporting clerks and the district attorney. This is local justice-system financing.

Expands or revises Tuscaloosa County pretrial diversion while providing for fees, costs, and restitution. It offers an alternative to prosecution but finances access partly through participant charges.
Authorizes a Jefferson County business-license tax with exceptions and limits, providing local general-fund revenue through business taxation.
Authorizes additional Cleburne County court costs in traffic cases. This is a local defendant fee.
Authorizes the Tuscaloosa County district attorney to employ investigators. This is local prosecutorial capacity.
Reallocates Jackson County TVA payments among the legislative office, schools, municipalities, and a discretionary committee. This is local revenue distribution.
Alters Gulf Shores' municipal boundaries. This is local geography.
Adds a Wilcox County service-of-process fee for law enforcement. This is local user-fee financing.
Allows Internet or mail tag renewal in Wilcox County with a transaction fee. This is local administrative access and user charging.
Allows online property-tax payment in Wilcox County with a transaction fee. This is local administrative access and user charging.
Allows online property-tax payment in Lowndes County with a transaction fee. This is local administrative access and user charging.
Allows Internet or mail tag renewal in Lowndes County with a transaction fee. This is local administrative access and user charging.

Revises Colbert County diversion eligibility, covered offenses, and fees. The program remains a prosecution alternative, but the synopsis does not state whether particular eligibility expands or contracts.
Allows the Legislature to provide alternate local election officers by local law. This is election staffing procedure without a stated access effect.
Limits covered public-housing authorities' land purchases to public-housing purposes and requires notice to surrounding owners, constraining authority discretion and expanding neighborhood notice.
Requires municipal-council approval before a public-housing authority uses eminent domain, adding elected oversight and restricting condemnation autonomy.
Allows draft or keg beer sales in Daleville subject to voter approval, a local alcohol liberalization.
Allows draft or keg beer sales in Ozark subject to voter approval, a local alcohol liberalization.
Joins an interstate compact standardizing insurance-product regulation, favoring multistate regulatory coordination and streamlined product approval.
Creates a multistate surplus-lines insurance compliance compact, centralizing and standardizing regulation across states.

Extends child controlled-substance exposure law to a child in utero, fixes venue, and creates an exposure presumption from a positive test at birth. It expands punitive pregnancy regulation and embeds fetal personhood in criminal child-protection law.
Allows fractional teacher units to be combined and unused fractions to support salaries and benefits, expanding local flexibility in education staffing funds.
Adds the Building Commission director to the energy and residential codes board. This is administrative representation.
Allows unemployment benefits for military spouses who leave work to follow station, activation, or deployment orders, expanding worker income protection for military families.

Substantially revises funeral-establishment and mortuary regulation while raising application, renewal, inspection, and violation charges. It strengthens occupational and consumer-protection enforcement at higher regulated-party cost.
Allows people outside Alabama on military or mission assignment to declare state residency for non-election purposes while expressly preventing the declaration from establishing voting eligibility.
Authorizes district attorneys to appoint investigators with law-enforcement duties and powers, expanding prosecutorial capacity.

Limits both grandparents' visitation petitions and parents' amendment or revocation petitions to defined 24-month intervals. It prioritizes finality and reduced litigation rather than consistently favoring either parental or grandparent rights.
Mourns Franklin County tornado deaths and commends survivors, volunteers, and donors. This is commemorative.

Requires an online statewide database of public-contract bids and proposals, expanding procurement transparency and vendor access.
Requires rebate issuers to process submissions within a defined period and makes violations deceptive trade practices, strengthening consumer remedies.
Adopts a statutory perpetuities rule allowing trusts to delay vesting for up to 360 years, expanding long-term private control of wealth and property.
Removes constitutional provisions concerning poll taxes and racially segregated schools, advancing formal racial civil rights and constitutional cleanup even though the provisions were unenforceable.
Adds cathinone compounds to Schedule I, subjecting them to controlled-substance regulation and criminal penalties.
Preempts local fertilizer regulation and reserves the field to the Agriculture Department subject to an exception, restricting local environmental authority.
Creates or clarifies a voluntary income-tax-refund contribution supporting firefighters' annuity benefits.
Adds organized volunteer-fire-department representation to the standards commission in place of a gubernatorial appointee. This is stakeholder governance.

Enacts the annual General Fund operating budget. The title provides no line-item changes from a baseline, so bill-level ideological direction cannot be inferred without a separate appropriations analysis.
Creates online insurance verification before registration and for law enforcement, strengthening compulsory auto-insurance enforcement through integrated data access.
Establishes a committee and statutory mechanism for state reimbursement of election expenses, strengthening support for local election administration.
Adds a military-officers association to organizations nominating members of the Veterans' Affairs Board. This is stakeholder representation.
Requires periodic compliance feedback and recommendations for unsupervised status for qualifying probationers, expanding earned supervision relief and rehabilitation incentives.
Allows the Pharmacy Board to regulate repackaging and storage of unused noncontrolled prescription drugs in residential-care facilities, reducing waste under professional safeguards.

Further provides for paying Veterans' Affairs employee salaries and expenses from the General Fund. This supports state veterans-service administration, though the title does not quantify a funding change.

Reduces the Corrections General Fund appropriation, substitutes departmental and federal bonus funds, and makes supplemental appropriations to Medicaid, senior, human-services, mental-health, health, rehabilitation, youth, parole, ethics, audit, and military agencies. It reallocates fiscal resources from prison general funding toward a broad service portfolio rather than simply increasing total spending.
Moves specified Jefferson County jobs from classified service to at-will status while addressing return rights and benefits, weakening merit-system protection for those positions.
Prohibits altering boat, motor, part, and trailer identification and adds possession penalties and forfeiture, expanding property-crime enforcement and asset seizure.
Prohibits animal shelters from euthanizing cats and dogs in gas chambers after a delayed effective date, strengthening humane-treatment standards.
Prohibits private obligations imposing fees on future real-property transfers and supplies enforcement rules, restricting long-lived private encumbrances.

Reorganizes the Alabama Development Office as a Commerce Department and authorizes selected employment outside the Merit System, combining economic-development centralization with weaker civil-service coverage.
Authorizes local warning signs on residential roads for children who are deaf or blind, supporting disability safety accommodation.
Generally bars product-liability relief against sellers that did not manufacture the product, limiting consumer tort remedies and retail liability.
Authorizes electronic citations and summonses for misdemeanor nontraffic violations, modernizing lower-level criminal procedure without increasing the offense classification.
Exempts qualifying retired service members and reservists from distinctive-tag taxes and registration fees, expanding targeted veterans' relief.
Further regulates admissibility of expert opinions, adopting a stronger judicial gatekeeping approach that tends to restrict unsupported expert evidence and can narrow civil claims.
Requires agencies to adopt written internal-investigation rules and provide them to officers, expanding procedural protection and predictability for law-enforcement employees.
Expands tastings, sampling, cross-manufacturer beer sales, brewpub purchasing, and permissible locations subject to tax collection, liberalizing regulated alcohol commerce.

Expedites disposition of seized fighting dogs, requires owners to post care bonds in covered cases, and authorizes forfeiture, strengthening animal-welfare enforcement with property and due-process consequences.
Creates a crime for filing a false lien against a public officer or employee, expanding protection against retaliatory paper harassment.
Annexes Lake View's municipal complex. This is local geography.
Revises publication or posting rules for municipal planning, zoning, licensing, and other ordinances. The title does not establish whether public notice strengthens or weakens.
Revises publication of port-authority bond notices and limits the period for civil challenges, favoring faster finality for public development debt.

Reduces statutory interest on noncontract money judgments from 12 percent to 7.5 percent while specifying daily computation and annual compounding. The principal distributive effect favors judgment debtors and reduces the value and collection leverage of civil awards.
Imposes and distributes a Perry County lodging tax, a local consumption-tax and revenue measure.

Raises mandatory imprisonment for protection-order violations and extends enforcement to orders issued by tribes and U.S. territories, expanding punitive domestic-violence protection and interjurisdictional recognition.
Allows the personal representative to file where the deceased could have sued if living, clarifying or broadening venue access for wrongful-death claims.

Allows local education boards to issue interest-bearing warrants with state approval, sell them publicly or privately, and exempt principal and interest from tax, expanding education debt-financing flexibility.
Recodifies municipal fine provisions while repealing a superseded section. No amount or penalty-direction change is stated.
Transfers regulation of covered private water systems supplied by municipalities from the Public Service Commission to municipal government, expanding local utility control.
Requires corrupt intent to establish prohibited giving, solicitation, or receipt under the ethics provision, narrowing liability and protecting conduct lacking a quid-pro-quo purpose.

Allows recyclers to acquire low-value salvage vehicles without title while requiring ownership statements, identifiers, and lien checks with penalties. It reduces title formalities while adding anti-theft safeguards.
Allows counties and municipalities to create public tourism-promotion authorities, expanding local economic-development institutions.
Increases the penalty for possessing gambling devices, strengthening vice and public-morality enforcement.
Appropriates funds to the Coalition Against Domestic Violence subject to operational and audited reporting, supporting victim services with accountability conditions.
Appropriates tobacco-settlement revenue to Children First programs subject to revenue availability, audits, and legislative reporting, supporting children's services with fiscal controls.
Defines the crimes constituting moral turpitude for voting disqualification, replacing indeterminate case-by-case exclusion with an enumerated scope and improving restoration clarity.
Delays an existing Garrett Coliseum renovation appropriation from fiscal 2012 to 2013. This changes timing rather than adopting a new subsidy.
Extends transfers from road and bridge funds to Public Safety operations while postponing authority to buy traffic-enforcement vehicles, reallocating transportation money toward agency operations.
Creates licensure and road-use rules for low-speed vehicles and mini-trucks, requires safety equipment, and waives titles. It liberalizes use subject to safety regulation.
Appropriates funds to the Kidney Foundation subject to operating plans, audits, and periodic reports, supporting public-health services with accountability.
Exempts compensation earned by Alabama military personnel deployed to combat or hazardous-duty areas from state income tax, expanding targeted service-member relief.
Expands grandparent-visitation law to great-grandparents and revises best-interest considerations, broadening relatives eligible to seek court-ordered access.

Classifies administrative and technical probation violations and defines eligible and nonviolent offenders, supporting graduated sanctions rather than treating all noncompliance as equivalent to new criminal conduct.
Creates a comprehensive Insurance Department licensing and regulatory regime for insurance adjusters, expanding occupational oversight.
Creates territorial, termination, inventory-repurchase, and warranty rules protecting recreational-vehicle dealers and constraining manufacturers.

Requires banks to be organized under general law, permits unlimited duration, and prohibits political subdivisions from owning bank stock or lending credit, favoring standardized private banking and limiting public ownership.
Exempts licensed professional counselors and churches or ministries providing religious services from Mental Health Department licensure, reducing regulation for professional and religious providers.
Requires funding-source disclosure for electioneering communications and paid political advertising and revises committee contribution rules, expanding campaign-finance transparency.
Removes the requirement that a commercial driver carry and produce metal-coil load-securement certification in the vehicle, reducing paperwork while leaving underlying securement rules intact.
Allows the Senate President Pro Tempore to spend unexpended fiscal-year funds without existing restrictions, expanding leadership budget discretion and weakening earmark controls.
Provides a vehicle allowance for the Lee County coroner. This is local compensation.
Abolishes the Lee County constable office. This is local governmental structure.
Creates a Human Resources Department individual-development-account program for low-income residents, expanding asset-building support.
Creates a comprehensive adult and juvenile sex-offender registration and notification regime, limits residence and employment, and authorizes fees, substantially expanding punitive supervision.
Defines a person to include every human from fertilization, advancing a fetal-personhood rule associated with restricting abortion and some reproductive technologies.

Repeals the Teacher Tenure and Fair Dismissal Acts and replaces them with the Students First framework, reducing established employment protections and expanding management flexibility over education personnel.
Expressly authorizes courts to fine and imprison people held in contempt for failure to pay child support, expanding coercive enforcement of family-support obligations.
Creates an interagency elder-abuse prevention council with reporting duties, expanding coordinated protection of vulnerable adults.
Eliminates de novo circuit-court review of Class 2 municipal liquor-license decisions, increasing municipal finality and narrowing applicant judicial recourse.

Retains tenant recovery for prohibited lease terms and expressly allows tenant attorney fees for landlord noncompliance, but also expands reciprocal landlord fees and remedies, defines drug use, firearm discharge outside self-defense, and other acts as noncurable defaults permitting seven-day termination, and clarifies abandonment recovery. The overall package materially strengthens landlord enforcement while preserving selected tenant remedies.
Changes appointment, voting, and meeting rules for Birmingham's racing commission. This is local governance.

Clarifies disability definitions and accessible-space design, prohibits restrictions on public-transportation access, and lets municipalities deputize parking enforcers, strengthening disability accommodation and enforcement.
Creates licensing and regulation for real-estate appraisal management companies, expanding professional and consumer-protection oversight.
Alters Piedmont's municipal boundaries. This is local geography.
Appropriates funds to children's advocacy centers subject to plans, audits, and reports, supporting child-abuse response services with accountability.

Redirects $5 million otherwise earmarked annually for state parks and $1 million otherwise earmarked annually for Coastal Programs to the General Fund in fiscal 2012 and 2013. It temporarily reduces protected conservation funding to increase unrestricted budget flexibility.

Creates a statewide Indigent Defense Services Office with staff and circuit advisory boards and formalizes appointed, contract, and public-defender systems and compensation. It expands institutional support and oversight for the constitutional right to counsel.
Creates a commission to make quadrennial legislative-compensation and expense recommendations and repeals prior compensation statutes, reducing legislators' direct control over their own pay.
Repeals required Education Trust Fund and General Fund matching transfers to the Penny Trust Fund for health care, reducing a dedicated public-health funding mechanism.
Revises Lee County fire-district dwelling definitions, rates, emergency medical services, paid staffing, and ballots. This is local emergency-service governance and finance.
Directs Morgan County TVA payments to local school boards for fiscal 2012 and 2013. This is local education-funding allocation.

Expands state elevator safety and private-residence inspection authority, permits unsafe elevators to be taken out of service, and preempts local regulation. It strengthens centralized safety enforcement while restricting local control.

Allows health professionals, institutions, and payers to decline services conflicting with conscience and supplies injunctive relief. It expands religious and moral refusal rights while restricting patient access to reproductive, end-of-life, or other contested care.
Authorizes merger of Prichard's water and sewer board into the Mobile-area system with assumption of assets and debt. This is local utility restructuring.
Directs a portion of Marshall County TVA payments to local education boards. This is local education-funding allocation.
Continues Lauderdale County's solicitor fee while repealing a superseded local act. This is local court financing.
Creates procedures for transferring estate, trust, guardianship, and conservatorship matters between probate and circuit courts, improving jurisdictional administration and access.
Adds Lauderdale County court costs supporting the regional drug task force. This is a local defendant fee and enforcement appropriation.
Establishes pretrial diversion in the Eleventh Judicial Circuit, expanding alternatives to prosecution for eligible defendants.

Redraws congressional districts after the 2010 census. Partisan and racial consequences require a separate plan-level geographic analysis rather than inference from the title.
Allows counties to create public watershed-management corporations with boards, powers, staff, and state retirement and health benefits, expanding public regional water-resource governance.
Exempts farm-raised yellow perch from the sale prohibition, liberalizing commerce in privately raised fish.
Adds Marion County court costs in domestic-violence cases to support the Coalition Against Domestic Violence, combining a local defendant fee with victim-service funding.
Protects existing tax incentives and abatements for property damaged or destroyed by the April 2011 tornadoes, preventing disaster-related loss of economic-development benefits.
Reallocates Jackson County TVA payments among the legislative office, schools, municipalities, and a discretionary committee. This is local revenue distribution.
Preserves residential or homestead property-tax classification when property is damaged by a natural disaster, protecting homeowners from a disaster-triggered tax increase.
Revises Auburn University's trustee-selection process and repeals the prior amendment. The synopsis does not establish a durable ideological direction.
Redistributes an existing Jefferson County solicitor fee among circuit and municipal clerks and the district attorney. This is local court financing.
Continues a Hale County ad valorem tax for a jail and law enforcement while repealing a duplicative act. This is local taxation and public-safety funding.
Allows fractional teacher units to be combined and unused fractions to support salaries and benefits, expanding local flexibility in education staffing funds.
Adopts the Uniform Power of Attorney Act for minors, incapacitated people, and other principals, standardizing delegated decisionmaking and fiduciary safeguards.
Eliminates county-versus-at-large notary distinctions and consolidates notary law, reducing geographic barriers and modernizing administration.
Creates a process to assess and implement secure electronic voting for overseas voters, seeking expanded military and overseas access while retaining security review.
Shortens the statute of repose for claims against architects, engineers, and builders, expanding civil recourse and professional liability exposure.
Creates an income-tax-refund checkoff for voluntary contributions to the state Historic Preservation Fund.

Increases penalties and license revocation for DUI offenders with a blood-alcohol level of at least .15 and addresses driving intoxicated with a child passenger, expanding punitive road-safety enforcement.
Retroactively validates specified municipal annexations under defined conditions. This resolves local boundary legality.
Closes the Deferred Retirement Option Plan to new participation and limits interest on existing DROP accounts, reducing enhanced public-pension benefits and future liabilities.
Allows a limited secondary public-contract award to certified HUBZone or small-business firms, expanding targeted procurement opportunities for disadvantaged-area and small enterprises.
Limits landowner liability when property is leased for hunting or fishing, encouraging recreational access by reducing private tort exposure.

Allows a basic telephone carrier to avoid last-resort service obligations where a property owner or developer has arranged an alternative carrier, reducing universal-service duties in privately served developments.
Expands educational-benefit eligibility for disabled veterans, spouses, and children when the veteran was not an Alabama resident before service, subject to funding criteria.
Extends or clarifies immunity for sheriff employees, reducing civil-liability exposure for local law-enforcement personnel.
Substantially revises funeral-service regulation while raising licensing, inspection, and violation charges, strengthening occupational oversight at higher regulated-party cost.
Prohibits fraudulent phone-bank misrepresentation about candidates or committees and authorizes Attorney General enforcement, strengthening campaign integrity through speech-related fraud regulation.
Creates an offense for leaving a child unattended in a vehicle and grades punishment by repetition and injury or death, expanding child-safety criminal enforcement.

Limits economic-welfare emergency contracts exempt from prior review to 60 days, bars a second identical or substantially similar emergency contract within one year, and requires immediate committee notice and concurrent review of longer successor contracts. Adds a Washington County probate marriage fee and dedicates it to office modernization. This is local user-fee financing.
Clarifies and retroactively preserves juvenile-court jurisdiction over adoption, visitation, custody, support, and related matters, supporting continuity and access in family adjudication.
Deletes the prohibition on an alcohol licensee, agent, or employee working for another licensee, reducing industry employment regulation.
Allows alternate election officers to be appointed by local law. This is election staffing procedure.
Replaces the Revenue Department's internal administrative-law division with a Tax Appeals Commission, increasing institutional separation in taxpayer adjudication.
Provides state-paid continued health coverage to surviving spouses and dependents of covered public employees killed in the line of duty, expanding survivor benefits.
Creates a housing trust fund and advisory committee for low- and moderate-income households, expanding public affordable-housing infrastructure.

Modernizes producer licensing, adds address-change reporting, creates specialized statutory regimes, and repeals obsolete provisions. It generally strengthens and streamlines insurance occupational regulation.

Sets an aggregate principal limit for state general-obligation bonds while exempting issuance from other constitutional limitations, formalizing but potentially expanding debt capacity within the new cap.
Raises income eligibility and creates a uniform application process for age- and disability-based homestead exemptions, expanding targeted property-tax relief and administrative access.
Allows unemployment benefits for military spouses who leave work due to station, activation, or deployment orders, expanding worker protection for military families.
Provides active and retired service members free state-park admission on state and federal holidays, expanding a targeted veterans' benefit.
Revises a Montgomery County recording fee and dedicates it to probate record-system improvements. This is local user-fee financing.

Requires insurers to use death records, notify the Treasurer, and remit unclaimed life benefits or retained accounts with interest, strengthening beneficiary protection and unclaimed-property enforcement.
Removes specified property from Fort Payne. This is local geography.
Allows Fort Payne to authorize and regulate draft or keg beer sales, a local alcohol liberalization.

Redistributes collected remote-use-tax proceeds among the General Fund and named entities without changing the underlying tax rate. This is a fiscal-allocation measure whose beneficiaries require line-item treatment.
Adds a DeKalb County marriage-license fee supporting the county child-advocacy center. This is local user-fee and child-service funding.
Authorizes a marriage-related fee for the DeKalb probate judge. This is local office financing.
Exempts lower-paid public employees from statements of economic interests and allows covered gift receipt, reducing ethics disclosure and gift restrictions for that employee class.
Requires polygraph-examiner applicants to undergo state and national fingerprint background checks, tightening occupational screening.
Allows presiding circuit judges to conduct specified civil hearings by audio-video communication, expanding remote court access.
Places the gun-show business-license tax on the organizer rather than participants under covered conditions, consolidating tax administration without changing firearm rights.
Extends existing development tax incentives to coal-mining companies, providing targeted fiscal support to fossil-fuel extraction.
Extends coal excise and privilege taxes and revises proceeds distribution, preserving an industry-specific charge and public revenue stream.
Expands chiropractic licensing and clinic-permit regulation through fingerprinting, exams, subpoena authority, discipline and fee rules, strengthening professional oversight and entry requirements.
Creates procedures for consumers to place and lift credit-report security freezes with notice, fees, and enforcement, expanding identity-theft protection.
Reorganizes the development office as a Commerce Department and permits selected non-merit employment, combining economic-development centralization with weaker civil-service coverage.
Adds and revises orthotic-fitter and supplier definitions and licensing provisions, extending or clarifying professional regulation of these services.
Exempts veterinarians employed by qualifying nonprofits from specified employment and ownership restrictions, reducing professional-practice barriers for charitable veterinary care.
Adds cathinones, synthetic cannabinoids, and controlled analogs to regulated schedules and trafficking penalties, expanding punitive drug prohibition.
Prohibits clothing that exposes underwear in Montgomery public places and imposes civil penalties, using public-order authority to regulate personal dress and expression.
Creates conditional tax incentives for qualifying development and expansion projects based on job creation or retention, expanding targeted industrial subsidies.
Authorizes the University of South Alabama president to employ police officers, expanding campus law-enforcement capacity.
Allows University of South Alabama trustees to participate remotely under specified conditions, modernizing board access.

Creates an impaired-professional wellness program, changes physical-therapist assistants from registration to licensure, and revises board staffing, expanding professional support and regulatory gatekeeping.
Creates a homeowners bill of rights and makes violations unfair trade practices, expanding policyholder information and consumer remedies.
Caps a bar pilot's bond liability at $5,000 absent gross negligence, substantially limiting ordinary-negligence recovery.
Criminalizes false removal and filing of recorded instruments, including false filings against public officials, expanding fraud and anti-harassment enforcement.

Allows officers to request a license and issue an unlicensed-driving citation based on reasonable suspicion without personally observing the driving, expanding police investigatory and citation authority.
Raises the Dale County sheriff's salary and expense allowance. This is local compensation.
Allows the Dale County sheriff to operate a jail store and use proceeds for law enforcement subject to audit. This is local correctional finance.

Creates hearings and witness notice when youthful-offender status is sought for intentional serious injury or death, placing heightened procedural and victim-oriented scrutiny on leniency for serious offenses.
