Creates a Hale County sheriff service-of-process fund, contracting authority, and fees.
Authorizes local background checks and fees by the Hale County sheriff.
Changes Municipal Electric Authority board size, compensation, and auditing arrangements without a clear policy direction.
Creates a Revenue Department amnesty program for delinquent taxpayers, reducing penalties to encourage voluntary compliance.
Requires Transportation fleet vehicles bought with state funds to come from Alabama dealerships, favoring local businesses over open procurement.
Criminalizes taking consigned motor fuel without owner consent or written agreement, strengthening property and commercial enforcement.
Bars homeowners and similar associations from restricting the design of modestly sized for-sale signs and creates damages, strengthening owner marketing rights over association control.
Allows cosmetologists to use neck brushes, removing a narrow practice restriction.
Allows cosmetology and barber schools to provide training above the secondary level.
Requires tax amnesty programs across 2015 through 2017, excluding fuel tax, reducing delinquency penalties to encourage compliance.
Replaces probate-issued marriage licensing with recording of a marriage contract and vital-statistics transmission, reducing official discretion over marriage recognition.
Expands when alcohol-status referendums may be held, increasing local democratic access to wet-dry decisions.

Allows two additional exempt employees per agency, expanding appointment and dismissal discretion, while preserving salary, benefits, and return rights for classified employees serving temporarily outside merit service.
Requires manufacturers to provide in-service training and ownership-change notice, strengthening emergency-device readiness.
Allows agencies funded by retained fees to raise them by CPI through rulemaking every five years, expanding automatic user-fee authority.
Allows the Labor Department to sue employers in the county of violation to collect assessed child-labor penalties, strengthening enforcement.
Removes temporary calendar parameters and lets local boards satisfy a 1,080-hour standard.
Creates default inheritance and ownership consequences for specified inter-vivos assets after divorce or annulment, aligning transfers with presumed post-divorce intent.
Creates electronic county filing for business entities, modernizing and easing compliance.
Extends National Guard plate exemptions and permits electronic insurance proof and Revenue notices.
Creates a criteria-based commission able to recommend or implement shifts in judgeships, expanding systematic court-resource allocation.
Creates a trust structure for settlement proceeds, repays rainy-day borrowing, and allocates interest among public funds, emphasizing fiscal reserves and capital investment.
Bars municipalities from narrowing state exemptions for work on private residences, preempting local contractor regulation.
Requires a subcontractor seat on the General Contractors Board, expanding small-contractor representation.
Adds Nursing Board members and changes nominations without a disclosed substantive policy direction.
Creates expedited title-clearing for tax-sale properties in Class 5 municipalities, a locally targeted redevelopment procedure.
Requires exemption certificates and Revenue reporting for sales and lodging taxes, strengthening tax-compliance verification.
Requires an administrative process before closing state parks or offices, constraining abrupt executive closure and protecting public recreation.
Transfers specified career-center-system entities or functions to the Labor Department, an administrative reorganization.
Moves the presidential primary to the first Tuesday in March, a calendar change without inherent ideological direction.
Replaces a broader good-standing certificate with tax-compliance certification, narrowing and clarifying a business filing prerequisite.
Allows retailers and state liquor stores to conduct tastings, expanding regulated alcohol promotion.
Combines and modernizes constitutional separation-of-powers language without a disclosed substantive change.

Makes the Surface Mining Commission's specialized hearing and appeal process supersede the Alabama Administrative Procedure Act and places judicial review in the circuit court where the commission has its principal office. This changes forum and review procedure without itself relaxing or strengthening mining standards, so it should not receive a substantive ideological direction.
Adds criminal-history checks, fees, qualification changes, and higher penalties for psychologists, strengthening occupational regulation.
Extends insurance discounts statewide for storm-resilient retrofits, incentivizing private mitigation investment.
Alters Alexander City's corporate limits, a local annexation measure.
Requires organizations receiving special sales-tax exemptions to report annually to Revenue, expanding tax-expenditure transparency.
Requires in-state escrow, limits withdrawals, and mandates notice for condominium deposits, strengthening buyer financial protection.
Authorizes Sunday-sales referendums in St. Clair County and its municipalities.
Adjusts the effective date for a Tuscaloosa County road-improvement commission.
Repeals and reenacts constitutional impeachment provisions, restructuring process without a clean issue-valence direction.
Creates public financing for grocery stores in underserved low- and moderate-income areas.
Authorizes preference for veterans in state hiring and promotion, expanding a military-service employment benefit.
Allows additional third-party agents and private-school instructors to administer driver examinations, expanding privatized licensing services.
Adopts the uniform interstate support act for recognizing, enforcing, and modifying foreign orders, strengthening cross-border child-support collection.
Expressly permits private employers to adopt voluntary veterans preferences, expanding lawful military-service preference.

Replaces fixed constitutional exemption provisions with a requirement that the Legislature establish homestead and personal-property exemptions by general law and preserves written waiver. It retains the protection while transferring its amount and conditions from the Constitution to ordinary legislation; that institutional tradeoff has no reliable scalar ideological direction.

Bars vision plans from setting prices for noncovered services, tying panel participation to another plan, restricting suppliers or optical labs, or using nominal reimbursement to evade the rule. The operative direction protects optometrist and ophthalmologist commercial autonomy against insurer contracting control.
Gives adult inmate training priority at the Frank Lee Youth Center, shifting correctional education resources toward adult rehabilitation.
Allows drivers to show insurance on a phone or electronic device, reducing paper-document requirements.
Expressly allows seasonal religious displays, protecting public religious expression.
Requires amendments and referendums to appear at statewide primary or general elections, increasing typical turnout while eliminating stand-alone timing flexibility.
Changes DeKalb County vacancy and special-election procedures.
Adds mandatory jail for repeat criminal mischief against churches and prioritizes restitution.
Revises Jacksonville State trustee membership and terms, an institutional governance change.
Creates a voluntary tax-refund contribution option for the USS Alabama Battleship Commission.
Criminalizes devices or software used to erase register sales, strengthening sales-tax enforcement.
Revises University of North Alabama trustee terms and permits teleconference meetings.
Allows consent-based electronic insurance delivery while preserving free paper copies, reducing mandated paper use with consumer choice.
Raises the Tallapoosa County sheriff's expense allowance and salary.
Provides a one-time additional payment to retirement-system retirees and beneficiaries.
Changes Jackson County TVA revenue uses for disaster relief and economic development.
Creates a petition process and burden of proof for court-ordered grandparent visitation, expanding third-party visitation.
Revises legislative procedure for classifying and adopting local constitutional amendments.
Revises membership of the Jefferson County pension board.
Creates a Jackson County service-of-process fee for failure-to-appear warrants.
Lets the Jackson County sheriff use inmate trust-account funds for law enforcement.
Expands disciplinary powers, definitions, fees, reciprocity, and prohibited activities under the plumbing and gas-fitting board.
Exempts Birmingham Zoo from state and local sales taxes, granting targeted public support to a nonprofit cultural institution.
Further structures the Manufactured Housing Commission advisory board without a disclosed substantive change.
Creates a St. Clair County booking fee for convicted defendants to fund county jails.
Allows federal or other state governments to perform Agriculture Department laboratory testing.
Authorizes the Sickle Cell Commission to make rules, expanding health-governance authority.
Exempts the Physical Therapy Board executive director from the state merit system, expanding appointment and dismissal discretion.
Authorizes additional road, bridge, and tunnel bonds and local funding agreements, expanding debt-financed transportation investment.
Broadens drag-racing crimes, raises penalties, and permits vehicle impoundment and repeat-offense forfeiture.
Revises local tax notices and authorizes specified Revenue collection services at no cost, expanding centralized compliance assistance.
Raises homestead and personal-property exemptions, protecting more debtor assets.

Replaces the recurring lowest-six-percent test with a school-grade rule based on an F or repeated Ds, with a lowest-ten-percent fallback if grading rules are unavailable. Because schools can enter or leave eligibility under the changed metric, the text does not establish a uniformly expansive or restrictive school-choice direction.
Creates a criteria-based commission able to shift judgeships, expanding systematic court-resource allocation.
Revises eligible tuition while requiring FAFSA submission, coordinating Guard assistance with federal aid but adding an application condition.
Changes Jefferson County civic-center board appointments by the legislative delegation.
Sets compensation and an expense allowance for the Montgomery County sheriff; this local compensation act is not a general ideological signal.
Authorizes active-duty service members to testify by video under defined conditions, expanding accommodation and access in judicial proceedings.
Authorizes municipal draft-beer sales only in Blount County; retain as a local alcohol act rather than a statewide ideology item.
Exempts specified insulin-pump and glucose-monitor manufacturers and distributors from home-medical-equipment licensure, narrowing occupational regulation for that market.
Extends responder-contractor civil immunity to additional hazardous-material and gasoline-spill response, limiting tort exposure for emergency work.
Sets the Lee County sheriff's salary and supplies no generalizable statewide policy direction.
Allows Lamar County officials to enter the regular employee retirement system instead of a local supernumerary program; this is a county-specific benefit structure.
Limits the special statutory liability for traps or similar devices to public land. This narrows a hunting-and-trapping liability rule, although the synopsis does not describe ordinary tort remedies.
Adds and distributes recording and tag fees for the Bullock County probate office; this is local revenue administration.
Creates a right for terminally ill patients to seek drugs or devices after Phase I testing under specified conditions, expanding patient access outside ordinary approval pathways.
Revises billboard definitions and spacing rules to conform with federal highway law. The synopsis supports a regulatory restructuring but not a confident broad deregulatory direction.
Prohibits nepotistic school hiring, strengthening public-integrity constraints on local education employment.
Reduces interest due on tax-sale property and therefore lowers the cost of redemption for owners or debtors seeking to recover the property.
Prohibits possession, purchase, sale, or use of powdered alcohol and attaches penalties, combining a product ban with punitive enforcement.
Expands fees, reapplication rules, and disciplinary regulation for assisted-living administrators, increasing occupational oversight.

Enumerates enforceable noncompetition, nonsolicitation, no-hire, exclusive-dealing, goodwill-sale, and dissolution covenants; creates presumptively reasonable durations; and permits judicial reformation of overbroad restraints. Although it preserves burdens, hardship defenses, and limited exceptions, its central effect strengthens and regularizes employer enforcement while restricting worker mobility.
Changes municipal license-plate issuance fees and commissions in Jefferson County; this is local fiscal administration.
Authorizes state entities to unearmark receipts and redirect them to areas with funding reductions, weakening dedicated-fund constraints while increasing administrative budget flexibility.

Removes probate judges from issuing marriage licenses and substitutes a recorded marriage contract. The institutional change also accommodates officials objecting to license issuance, but does not itself change which couples may marry; it should not be forced into a single scalar social-policy direction.
Expands entertainment-district alcohol rules only for Hoover and Vestavia Hills; classify as local rather than statewide ideology.

Redirects Forever Wild trust payments to state parks while prohibiting new land acquisition. It supports existing park operations but restricts conservation acquisition, so both dimensions must remain visible.
Revises how county and municipal solid-waste programs collect and use funds. The synopsis does not establish a substantive expansion or contraction of environmental service.
Broadens massage-therapy board regulation and raises penalties, strengthening occupational licensing and enforcement.
Creates and revises a qualified-depository mechanism for local textbook purchasing. This is procurement administration without a clear ideological direction.
Adds or revises an income-tax refund checkoff benefiting the Children's First Trust Fund, expanding a voluntary public collection channel for that program.

Revises wildlife-exhibition regulation and authorizes an additional fee. It increases the regulatory funding burden, while the title does not show whether substantive exemptions broaden or narrow overall.
Allows school boards to transport students to extracurricular activities by means other than a bus, expanding local operational flexibility.
Imposes and distributes an additional Jackson County sales and use tax subject to referendum; preserve as a local fiscal act.
Authorizes and distributes an additional Russell County vehicle-license issuance fee; this is county-specific finance.
Requires motorists passing bicycles to maintain at least three feet, expanding a road-safety mandate protecting cyclists.
Deletes Anniston's three-year accountant rotation restriction, a city-specific contracting rule without a generalizable statewide signal.
Creates the offense of homicide by vehicle or vessel and associated penalties, a direct punitive criminal-law expansion.
Adds district attorneys and circuit clerks to an elected-official judicial retirement structure and provides a death benefit, expanding public retirement coverage.
Joins an interstate compact seeking an Article V convention to require a federal balanced budget, advancing a binding constitutional fiscal constraint.
Repeals Bibb County rules governing commission meetings and work on private property; the local act is not suitable for statewide ideology scoring.
Authorizes Sunday and draft-beer sales in Millbrook under local exceptions; retain as a municipal alcohol act.
Repeals the Bibb County medical-examiner enabling act; this county institutional change is non-generalizable.
Constitutionally authorizes the Legislature to provide a retirement system for district attorneys and circuit clerks, enabling expanded public retirement coverage.
Requires a multi-year tax amnesty program excluding fuel taxes, reducing penalties or enforcement exposure for qualifying delinquent taxpayers who come into compliance.

Replaces narrower triggers based principally on a majority of priority schools or accreditation action with material academic, financial, organizational, operational, safety, governance, or accountability noncompliance and student benchmark failure. This expands and specifies the circumstances supporting state intervention while retaining notice and response procedures.
Adds qualifications, continuing education, and compensation rules for the Bibb County sheriff; this is a county office act.
Creates a remittance method for non-nexus sellers collecting use tax for Alabama customers, expanding remote-sales tax collection through a simplified system.
Authorizes Cullman County park fees, contest prizes, and a local disbursement fund; this is local park administration.

Allows increases in driver-license and identification-card fees subject to the Administrative Procedure Act and credits in specified cases, combining a higher user-fee authority with formal rulemaking safeguards.
Requires appeals from county human-resources departments to be filed only where that department is located, narrowing appellants' venue options.
Revises membership and office-supply spending for the Cullman County Community Development Commission; this is local governance.
Redistributes Etowah County sales and use tax proceeds among named local entities, making it unsuitable for statewide ideology scoring.
Expands alcoholic-beverage sales authority for entertainment districts or brewpubs, liberalizing regulated market access.
Changes Alabama State University's board size, terms, nominations, remote participation, and compensation. This is a governance redesign without a dependable scalar ideological direction.
Authorizes the conservation department to close areas to commercial and recreational shrimp harvesting, including by emergency rule, expanding resource-protection regulatory authority.
Creates wine supplier-wholesaler franchise protections only in Lee County. Its geographically bespoke commercial rules should not enter statewide ideology scores.
Exempts qualifying dump trucks from axle-spacing requirements, relaxing a commercial transportation restriction while leaving weight rules otherwise in place.
Authorizes DeKalb County and its municipalities to permit and regulate wind-energy systems. This is a county-specific siting regime rather than a general statewide ideological vote.

Revises review of administrative-rule disapprovals and the prospective application of a recently enacted procedure. This concerns interbranch rule-review mechanics rather than a substantive regulatory direction.
Alters the corporate limits of Section and has no generalizable statewide policy content.

Allows DHR to bypass otherwise required family-preservation efforts when parental methamphetamine or drug conditions are present. It strengthens protective intervention while reducing the procedural protection favoring reunification.
Redistributes Sumter County hazardous- and solid-waste fees and repeals a prior local act; retain as local fiscal administration.
Phases the Autauga County sheriff from a supernumerary program into the employee retirement system. This is a local office-benefit transition.
Allows the House Speaker and Senate President Pro Tempore to appoint designees on multimember bodies, changing representation mechanics without a substantive ideological direction.
Authorizes Sunday alcohol sales in Wetumpka under local exceptions; do not generalize it statewide.
Changes operation and compensation of the Baldwin County revenue commissioner's office; this is local administration.
Eliminates specified exemptions from the contractor gross-receipts privilege tax, broadening its base, and revises distribution of the proceeds.
Lets the Legislative Council determine timing for transfers of legislative-branch functions under a prior reorganization act. This is implementation procedure.
Authorizes draft-beer sales in Wetumpka with local exceptions; classify as a local alcohol act.
Adds administrative dissolution authority for noncompliant business entities and revises filing fees, strengthening entity-reporting enforcement.
Allows the Bullock County probate judge to process ad valorem taxes, a county office assignment without statewide ideological content.
Authorizes a Macon County gasoline and motor-fuel tax and its local enforcement and distribution; preserve as local fiscal policy.
Creates a Lee County legislative-delegation office funded through additional court costs; this is geographically specific institutional finance.
Adds child camp facilities to the 2,000-foot sex-offender residence exclusion, expanding a punitive residency restriction.
Extends or updates junkyard regulation adjacent to the national highway system, expanding highway-corridor land-use regulation for federal conformity.
Allows the Hale County Commission to set additional probate issuance fees; this is a local user-fee measure.
Creates factor-presence nexus thresholds subjecting nonresident individuals and out-of-state businesses with sufficient Alabama activity to state income tax, broadening enforceable tax nexus.

Requires audited boards, agencies, or departments to pay examiner-set audit costs. It funds public accountability by shifting its expense to the audited entity, a mixed institutional and fiscal change rather than a simple spending direction.
Alters Homewood's corporate limits and contains no statewide ideological signal.
Raises bid-guarantee amounts for public works, increasing the financial qualification barrier imposed on prospective contractors while protecting procurement performance.
Extends the maximum age of the Tallapoosa County probate judge to 72 through a local constitutional amendment.

Proposes unearmarking state revenue sources and unifying General Fund and Education Trust Fund appropriations, substantially expanding annual legislative budget discretion while dissolving dedicated-fund boundaries.
Requires medical licensing rules to be certified and reviewed for anticompetitive effects by legislative staff and a joint committee, strengthening competition oversight of occupational regulation.
Authorizes referendum-approved fire-protection fees for specified Russell County property; this is local service finance.
Requires monthly animal-intake and disposition reports and public access on request, expanding transparency and accountability for shelters and animal-control facilities.

Allows existing electric suppliers to build additional transmission facilities connecting with other suppliers and creates dispute appeals, expanding interconnection authority within the regulated utility system.

Prohibits state agencies from changing rules, specifications, or requirements during a service project, protecting contractors from midperformance administrative changes while limiting agency flexibility.
Designates the brown shrimp as the official state crustacean and carries no substantive ideological direction.

Authorizes forfeiture of terrorism-derived property, victim and law-enforcement claims to proceeds, and civil damages. It expands punitive property seizure and civil liability while creating recovery avenues for injured parties.
Creates a Shelby County judicial-commission nomination process for probate-judge vacancies; this local selection rule should not enter statewide ideology scores.
Requires local school boards to offer eligible high-school students a virtual-school option, expanding publicly provided educational choice and delivery flexibility.
Creates finance-department facilities, leasing, construction, and energy-management divisions and transfers Building Commission duties. This is an administrative reorganization.
Allows qualifying students who transfer from a two-year to four-year public college to receive an associate degree after completing sufficient credits, expanding recognition of earned credentials.
Immunizes a manufacturer from liability for a product it did not design, manufacture, sell, or lease, limiting innovator or brand-name product-liability exposure.
Requires disabled-parking placards to display the holder's full name, facilitating identity-based enforcement while reducing privacy for disabled users.
Prohibits eminent domain from being used to acquire mortgages or deeds of trust, constraining public acquisition power and protecting private financial-property interests.
Creates Athens-specific weed-abatement, lien, and foreclosure procedures; retain as local nuisance administration.

Revises supernumerary status, salary caps, and county-commission removal authority for county tax officials. Its application is to local office structures and does not provide a stable statewide ideological signal.

Adds representation to water boards serving other counties, subjects members to ethics law, and requires notice and a hearing for rate increases, strengthening public-utility representation and accountability.
Allows Elba's city council to authorize draft-beer sales; this is a municipal alcohol measure.
Revises Calhoun County bingo definitions and proceeds rules; this geographically specific gaming act is non-generalizable.

Allows local boards of education to conduct specified financial transactions electronically and repeals obsolete procedures. This modernizes administration without a substantive ideological direction.
Renames H. Councill Trenholm State Technical College as a community college; this institutional naming change is non-scoring.
Establishes a state palliative-care and quality-of-life advisory council and health-department program, expanding public health coordination and information infrastructure.

Combines unrelated clarifications governing county-municipal contracts, family-member employment, self-funded insurance, annexed-road maintenance, and emergency-district employee bonding. The omnibus administrative package has no defensible single scalar direction.

Allows motorists without apparent injuries and transportation employees to move crash-disabled vehicles from roadways and immunizes authorized assistance, expanding incident-clearance authority while limiting responder liability.

Adds county-paid compensation for Pike County registrars; this is a local office-payment measure.
Raises fines for auctioneer-board violations and defines its quorum, strengthening occupational enforcement while clarifying governance.
Allows a Choctaw County revenue commissioner to receive benefits from two systems for separate service periods; this individualized local retirement measure is non-generalizable.
Authorizes referendum-approved draft-beer sales in Lexington on days other than Sunday and prescribes dispensing equipment; this is local alcohol regulation.
Revises boat registration identifiers and fees and directs part of fee receipts to state parks, combining administrative modernization with user-fee-supported park funding.
Exempts LifeSouth Community Blood Centers from tax, providing targeted nonprofit health-care tax relief.

Raises the civil jurisdictional limit of district courts while revising filing and docket fees. It expands access to the lower-cost court forum, but fee changes must remain a separate incidence dimension.
Requires legislative ratification of a tribal gaming compact through constitutional amendment, constraining executive compact authority and adding a legislative approval barrier to gaming expansion.
Deletes the rule that county-officer compensation increases under the Omnibus Pay Act be granted only at budget time, expanding local timing flexibility for public compensation increases.
Broadens massage-therapy board regulation and raises penalties, strengthening occupational licensing and enforcement.
Allows a six-year-old to enroll in first grade in the enrolling district under the revised rule, expanding enrollment flexibility at the statutory age threshold.

Clarifies physical-therapy board authority to adopt potentially anticompetitive rules when prioritizing patient safety and wellness, strengthening professional regulation while explicitly subordinating competition concerns.

Extends or revises contract duration, creates sole-source requirements, and permits GSA and nationwide cooperative purchasing. It expands procurement options while retaining targeted accountability rules.
Alters the corporate limits of Union and has no statewide ideological content.
Allows breweries and brewpubs to sell alcohol for off-premises consumption and deletes location restrictions, liberalizing producer market access.
Establishes procedures and official responsibilities for counting write-in votes, strengthening the administrative recognition of legally cast write-in ballots.
Authorizes specified filing and information funds to support Secretary of State administration. This is internal fund-use authority rather than a substantive policy position.
Requires qualifying commercial vehicles to use right lanes on specified highways except when passing, expanding traffic-flow regulation of heavy trucks.
Creates a Dale County sheriff service-of-process fee and dedicated local fund; this is local court finance.
Licenses and regulates public insurance adjusters and imposes fees, expanding occupational and consumer-protection oversight of claims representatives.
Authorizes a state electronic-poll-book pilot in place of printed voter lists, expanding election-administration modernization subject to implementation controls.
Requires an in-state escrow agent, limits withdrawals, and mandates notice under condominium law, strengthening purchaser financial protections.
Limits salary increases for cabinet, department-head, and assistant exempt positions to three percent annually, constraining executive-appointed compensation growth.
Revises the Women's Commission quorum for meetings and business, an internal governance rule without a substantive issue direction.
Creates additional biennial legislative sessions dedicated to appropriations, increasing formal legislative attention and control over state budgeting, although it does not dictate spending levels.
Prohibits status-based waiver of SNAP work requirements, restricting benefit access for otherwise waiver-eligible adults and strengthening work-conditioned eligibility.

Requires wireless providers to disclose customer location to law enforcement under specified emergency circumstances. It expands emergency investigative access while narrowing communications-location privacy.
Revises division of proceeds affected by tax abatements, but the title does not identify a changed tax burden or beneficiary. Treat as fiscal administration absent operative incidence details.
Harmonizes extensive partnership and LLC formation, operation, merger, and dissolution provisions. This is a commercial-code reorganization without a clear scalar regulatory direction.
Changes the ordering of offices and candidate names on ballots, an election-administration rule rather than an ideological access change on the synopsis.
Requires DHR to try to place an infant with the infant's dependent minor mother in foster care, strengthening family preservation within the child-welfare system.
Creates reporting pathways for suspected financial exploitation of vulnerable adults and immunizes qualifying disclosures, expanding elder protection and reporter safeguards.
Defines cargo theft and fifth-wheel tampering crimes and penalties, directly expanding punitive criminal law.
Requires Forestry Commission certification standards for volunteer fire departments and authorizes decertification, expanding public-safety quality regulation.
Requires public elementary schools to teach handwriting and cursive by the end of third grade, expanding state curricular prescription.
Appropriates Banking Assessment Fee Fund resources to the Banking Department, supporting state financial-regulatory operations.
Establishes Education Trust Fund-supported dental loans repayable through service in medically underserved areas, expanding workforce investment tied to a geographic service obligation.
Provides supplemental Advancement and Technology Fund money to the Department of Education, expanding public-education capital and technology resources.
Creates a public loan-repayment program for advanced-practice nurses, expanding state investment in health-care workforce supply.
Creates a Choctaw County sheriff service-of-process fee and local law-enforcement fund; this is county-specific finance.
Extends the motor-fuel-tax suspension for compressed and liquefied natural gas vehicle fuel, providing targeted alternative-fuel tax relief.
Requires governing-board members at colleges and universities to complete ethics training and file compliance forms, strengthening public-institution accountability.
Applies motor-fuel tax rules to fuel delivered to an Alabama destination, strengthening destination-based tax collection; the title does not specify a rate change.

Defines the moral-turpitude offenses that disqualify citizens from voting, replacing an indeterminate standard with an enumerated rule and expanding practical restoration for people whose convictions fall outside it.
Merges budget operations for the Lawrence County revenue commissioner and allocates expenses among taxing governments; this is local administration.
Allows medical-school universities to create authorities owning and operating health-care facilities, expanding public university institutional capacity in health services.
Creates a distinctive plate and annual fee supporting domestic-violence prevention programs, expanding a voluntary public funding channel.
Constitutionally prohibits transfers from state park funds to other public accounts, protecting earmarked park resources while constraining general budget flexibility.
Adds a Montgomery County tax on alcohol sold in state stores and directs it to the district attorney; this is local tax and justice finance.
Revises billboard definitions and spacing to conform to federal highway law. It changes regulatory treatment but the title alone does not prove broad expansion or contraction.
Creates a tick-borne-illness study commission and process for allocating university research money, expanding public health research coordination.
Exempts specified engine manufacturers and distributors from unfair-trade-practice provisions applicable to vehicle markets, narrowing statutory dealer or purchaser protections for that class.
Authorizes referendum-based Sunday alcohol sales in Southside; this is a local market-access measure.
Adds Shelby County probate recording fees to fund a legislative-delegation office; preserve as local institutional finance.
Establishes an enumerated moral-turpitude definition for voter disqualification, replacing a vague standard and expanding practical eligibility for citizens with nonlisted convictions.
Moves Fair Ballot Commission statements from the legislative website to the Secretary of State website, an administrative publication change.

Extensively revises captive-insurer licensing, taxation, and corporate requirements. Without operative deltas, the synopsis supports a sectoral restructuring but not a reliable scalar regulatory or tax direction.

Revises how a physician indicates that generic substitution is not allowed. It protects prescriber control over brand selection while restricting substitution and its potential cost savings when invoked.
Creates a Washington County sheriff service-of-process fee and dedicated law-enforcement fund; this is county-specific finance.
Authorizes a referendum on Sunday alcohol sales in Kellyton, a local market-access issue.

Clarifies Dental Examiners Board rulemaking authority in the antitrust-supervision context. This strengthens or protects professional self-regulation, though the title does not identify individual substantive rules.

Revises vehicle-title exemptions and involuntary transfers, requires Revenue Department notice, and adds dealer penalties, strengthening title-system compliance alongside administrative modernization.
Makes sewage discharge to the ground unlawful under the revised provision, strengthening direct environmental and public-health protection.
Creates a program allowing nonmedical persons to administer epinephrine auto-injectors, expanding emergency medication access and lay-responder authority.
Allows nonresident college students to buy resident hunting and fishing licenses other than lifetime licenses, reducing their user-fee burden and expanding access.
Requires municipal salary or expense increases to be introduced at least thirty days before adoption, strengthening notice and accountability for public compensation decisions.
Reserves seed regulation to the Department of Agriculture and preempts local rules, expanding statewide uniformity while eliminating local regulatory authority.
